Read it so you know what it does; you will explain it in your report.\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Status line for IPHS 400 MP2.\n\nClaude Code runs this script on every status-line refresh and pipes session\nJSON to stdin. The script does two things:\n  1. prints one line under the prompt:  [Opus] ctx 47% ▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░\n  2. records the context percentage in .claude/state/ctx_<session>.json so the\n     Stop hook (ctx_guard.py) can read it at the end of each turn.\nIt must never crash: a broken status line hides the meter, nothing else.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n\ndef project_dir(data: dict) -> Path:\n    ws = data.get(\"workspace\") or {}\n    return Path(\n        os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\")\n        or ws.get(\"project_dir\")\n        or ws.get(\"current_dir\")\n        or os.getcwd()\n    )\n\n\ndef bar(pct: float, width: int = 10) -> str:\n    filled = max(0, min(width, round(pct / 100 * width)))\n    return \"▓\" * filled + \"░\" * (width - filled)\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    try:\n        data = json.load(sys.stdin)\n    except Exception:\n        print(\"ctx ?\")\n        return\n\n    model = (data.get(\"model\") or {}).get(\"display_name\", \"Claude\")\n    pct = (data.get(\"context_window\") or {}).get(\"used_percentage\")\n    if pct is None:\n        print(f\"[{model}] ctx --\")\n        return\n    pct = float(pct)\n\n    session = data.get(\"session_id\") or \"default\"\n    state_dir = project_dir(data) / \".claude\" / \"state\"\n    try:\n        state_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        tmp = state_dir / f\"ctx_{session}.json.tmp\"\n        tmp.write_text(json.dumps({\"pct\": pct, \"ts\": time.time()}))\n        tmp.replace(state_dir / f\"ctx_{session}.json\")  # atomic swap\n    except OSError:\n        pass  # meter still prints even if the disk write fails\n\n    flag = \"  ⚠ compact at next green test\" if pct >= 60 else \"\"\n    print(f\"[{model}] ctx {pct:.0f}% {bar(pct)}{flag}\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n```\n\n## Step 4 — Write the Stop hook's logic (the exercise)\n\nThe template ships `ctx_guard.py` with everything written **except the body of `decide()`**, which raises `NotImplementedError`. Seven of the ten tests in `tests/test_ctx_guard.py` fail until you finish it. This is your first practice run of the loop on something tiny.\n\nIn a fresh Claude Code session:\n\n```text\n/clear\n/tdd Implement decide() in .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py so the failing tests in tests/test_ctx_guard.py pass. Do not change the tests or any other function.\n```\n\n`/tdd` runs the tests, watches them fail, writes the code, and runs them again until they pass. You do not type `pytest` yourself.\n\nThe rules `decide()` must follow:\n\n- Map the percentage to a band: 0 = below 50, 1 = 50+, 2 = 60+, 3 = 80+ (the thresholds come from `thresholds()`).\n- **Warn once per upward crossing.** Going from 52% to 55% must stay quiet.\n- **Re-arm after compaction.** When usage drops (after `/compact` or `/clear`), remember the lower band so the next crossing warns again.\n\nWhen the tests pass, compare your version with the complete file below.\n\n\n## Step 5 — Read the compaction logger\n\nThis file is complete. It writes the evidence the judge reads for rubric item B6.\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"PreCompact hook: log every compaction to docs/process/compaction-log.md.\n\nThis is grading evidence for rubric item B6 (session hygiene):\n  - trigger \"manual\" + a focus note  = you compacted on purpose (good)\n  - trigger \"auto\"                   = the session overflowed (fix the habit)\nNever exits 2: exit 2 on PreCompact would BLOCK compaction.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nHEADER = (\n    \"# Compaction log\\n\\n\"\n    \"| UTC time | Session | Trigger | Focus note |\\n\"\n    \"|---|---|---|---|\\n\"\n)\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    try:\n        event = json.load(sys.stdin)\n    except Exception:\n        return\n    project = Path(os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\") or event.get(\"cwd\") or os.getcwd())\n    log = project / \"docs\" / \"process\" / \"compaction-log.md\"\n    log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    if not log.exists():\n        log.write_text(HEADER)\n    note = (event.get(\"custom_instructions\") or \"\").replace(\"|\", \"/\").replace(\"\\n\", \" \").strip()\n    row = \"| {} | {} | {} | {} |\\n\".format(\n        datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M\"),\n        (event.get(\"session_id\") or \"?\")[:8],\n        event.get(\"trigger\", \"unknown\"),\n        note or \"(none)\",\n    )\n    with log.open(\"a\") as f:\n        f.write(row)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    try:\n        main()\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    sys.exit(0)\n```\n\n**Warning:** never change its exit code to 2. On `PreCompact`, exit code 2 **blocks compaction**, which would lock you inside an overflowing session.\n\n## Step 6 — Confirm the hooks are registered\n\nThe template already registers all three in `.claude/settings.json`, together with\nthe `SessionEnd` transcript saver. Read that file now so you know what is wired up:\n\n```bash\ncat .claude/settings.json\n```\n\n**Expected:** a `statusLine` entry plus `Stop`, `PreCompact`, and `SessionEnd`\nhooks, each pointing at a script in `.claude/hooks/`. Check it is valid JSON:\n\n```bash\npython3 -m json.tool .claude/settings.json > /dev/null && echo \"settings OK\"\n```\n\n**Expected:** `settings OK`. If you ever edit this file and see\n`Expecting ',' delimiter`, a comma is missing at the line number shown.\n\n## Step 7 — Keep the state files out of git\n\nThe meter's scratch files are per-session and per-laptop. They must not be committed:\n\n```bash\ngrep -qxF '.claude/state/' .gitignore || echo '.claude/state/' >> .gitignore\ntail -3 .gitignore\n```\n\n**Expected:** `.claude/state/` appears in the last lines. (`docs/process/compaction-log.md` *is* committed; it is evidence.)\n\n## Step 8 — Test the scripts without Claude\n\nPipe fake session data in, exactly as Claude Code would:\n\n```bash\nexport CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=\"$PWD\"\n\necho '{\"session_id\":\"demo\",\"model\":{\"display_name\":\"Opus\"},\"context_window\":{\"used_percentage\":63}}' \\\n  | python3 .claude/hooks/ctx_statusline.py\n\necho '{\"session_id\":\"demo\",\"hook_event_name\":\"Stop\"}' | python3 .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py\necho '{\"session_id\":\"demo\",\"hook_event_name\":\"Stop\"}' | python3 .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py\n\nrm -f .claude/state/ctx_demo*.json\n```\n\n**Expected output, in order:**\n\n1. `[Opus] ctx 63% ▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░░  ⚠ compact at next green test`\n2. `{\"systemMessage\": \"Context 63%: at the next green test run  /compact keep: ticket #N acceptance criteria, what is left, files touched\"}`\n3. *(nothing)*: the second call is silent because it already warned once.\n\n## Step 9 — Test it live with low thresholds\n\nStart Claude with thresholds so low that the first reply trips them:\n\n```bash\nCTX_WARN_PCT=1 CTX_COMPACT_PCT=2 claude\n```\n\n1. Look under the prompt. **Expected:** `[<model>] ctx N% ▓░░░░░░░░░`.\n2. Type `/hooks`. **Expected:** `Stop` and `PreCompact` each show 1+ hooks with the source `Project Settings`. Press Esc.\n3. Type `say hi`. After Claude answers, **expected:** a warning line starting `Context N%:`.\n4. Type `/compact keep: hook test`. Then open `docs/process/compaction-log.md`. **Expected:** a new row ending `| manual | keep: hook test |`.\n5. Type `/exit`. From now on start Claude normally (`claude`), and the real 50/60/80% thresholds apply.\n\nDelete the test row from `docs/process/compaction-log.md` so your log starts clean.\n\n## Step 10 — Commit\n\n```text\nCommit the context-threshold hooks, settings.json, .gitignore, and tests/test_ctx_guard.py with the message \"setup: context-threshold warning hook\" and push.\n```\n\nCheck on GitHub that the commit appears, and that `.claude/state/` is **not** in the repo.\n\n---\n\n## Using it during tickets\n\n| You see | Do this |\n|---|---|\n| Meter under 50% | Keep working. |\n| `Context 5x%: … plan a /compact` | Let the current red-green cycle finish. |\n| `Context 6x%: at the next green test run /compact keep: …` | As soon as the tests are green, type `/compact keep: ticket #N acceptance criteria, what is left, files touched` (with the real ticket number). |\n| `Context 8x%: compact now …` | Compact immediately, or `/handoff` and start a new session. Afterward, ask whether the ticket should be split with `/to-tickets`. |\n| A log row with trigger `auto` | The session overflowed and Claude compacted on its own. It is not an error, but the judge counts it against B6; next time, compact yourself at 60%. |\n| Starting the next short ticket | `/clear`. No compaction needed. |\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| No meter under the prompt | `statusLine` block missing, or JSON invalid | Rerun the Step 6 JSON check; restart Claude |\n| Meter shows `ctx --` | Your Claude Code version does not send `context_window` | Run `claude update`, restart |\n| Meter works, never any warning | Stop hook not registered, or the path is wrong | `/hooks` should list it; if it shows `Failed with non-blocking status code`, the path in `settings.json` is wrong |\n| `python3: command not found` inside the hook | Hook shell has a different PATH | Replace `python3` in `settings.json` with the full path from `which python3` |\n| Compaction log never appears | `PreCompact` entry missing | Recheck Step 6 with `/hooks` |\n| Focus note column says `(none)` | You ran `/compact` with no note, or your version names the field differently | Always type a note; if it still shows `(none)`, tell the instructor your `claude --version` |\n| Warnings pop up in the wrong pane | Should not happen: each session has its own state file | Delete `.claude/state/` and restart both sessions |\n\nIf none of these fix it, follow the self-help ladder in the manual: reread the error, run `/hooks`, ask Claude to explain the error before changing anything, check the [hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) and [status line docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline), log it with `/teach-log`, then email the instructor with the error pasted in.\n\n## Saved? The hook never blocks and never\nruns /compact itself: slash commands are yours to type.\n\nThresholds (override when launching:  CTX_WARN_PCT=1 claude  to test):\n  CTX_WARN_PCT     default 50  -> \"plan a /compact\"\n  CTX_COMPACT_PCT  default 60  -> \"/compact at the next green test\"\n  urgent = CTX_COMPACT_PCT + 20 -> \"compact or /handoff now; consider splitting\"\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nNONE, WARN, COMPACT, URGENT = 0, 1, 2, 3\n\n\ndef thresholds() -> tuple[float, float, float]:\n    warn = float(os.environ.get(\"CTX_WARN_PCT\", 50))\n    compact = float(os.environ.get(\"CTX_COMPACT_PCT\", 60))\n    return warn, compact, compact + 20\n\n\ndef band_for(pct: float, warn: float, compact: float, urgent: float) -> int:\n    if pct >= urgent:\n        return URGENT\n    if pct >= compact:\n        return COMPACT\n    if pct >= warn:\n        return WARN\n    return NONE\n\n\ndef message_for(band: int, pct: float) -> str:\n    p = f\"{pct:.0f}%\"\n    return {\n        WARN: (\n            f\"Context {p}: finish the current red-green cycle, then plan a \"\n            \"/compact at the next green test.\"\n        ),\n        COMPACT: (\n            f\"Context {p}: at the next green test run  /compact keep: ticket #N \"\n            \"acceptance criteria, what is left, files touched\"\n        ),\n        URGENT: (\n            f\"Context {p}: compact now (or /handoff and start fresh). If this \"\n            \"ticket keeps overflowing, split it with /to-tickets.\"\n        ),\n    }[band]\n\n\ndef decide(pct: float, last_band: int) -> tuple[str | None, int]:\n    \"\"\"Pure function (unit-tested): return (message or None, band to store).\n\n    Warn once per upward crossing. When usage drops (after /compact or\n    /clear), store the lower band so the next crossing warns again.\n    \"\"\"\n    raise NotImplementedError(\"MP2 Exercise A: implement me with /tdd\")\n\nLEDGER_COLUMNS = [\n    \"ts\", \"session\", \"phase\", \"provider\", \"model\", \"effort\",\n    \"ctx_pct\", \"five_h_pct\", \"weekly_pct\",\n]\n\n\ndef log_usage(project: Path, session: str, state: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Append one row per turn to notes/usage-ledger.csv (rubric item B7).\"\"\"\n    ledger = project / \"notes\" / \"usage-ledger.csv\"\n    phase_file = project / \".claude\" / \"state\" / \"phase\"\n    try:\n        phase = phase_file.read_text().strip() or \"unlabelled\"\n    except OSError:\n        phase = \"unlabelled\"\n\n    def cell(value: object) -> str:\n        return \"\" if value is None else str(value)\n\n    row = [\n        datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(\"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ\"),\n        session[:8], phase, cell(state.get(\"provider\")), cell(state.get(\"model\")),\n        cell(state.get(\"effort\")), f\"{float(state.get('pct', 0)):.1f}\",\n        cell(state.get(\"five_h\")), cell(state.get(\"weekly\")),\n    ]\n    try:\n        ledger.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        new = not ledger.exists()\n        with ledger.open(\"a\", newline=\"\") as f:\n            writer = csv.writer(f)\n            if new:\n                writer.writerow(LEDGER_COLUMNS)\n            writer.writerow(row)\n    except OSError:\n        pass\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    try:\n        event = json.load(sys.stdin)\n    except Exception:\n        return\n    project = Path(os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\") or event.get(\"cwd\") or os.getcwd())\n    session = event.get(\"session_id\") or \"default\"\n    state_dir = project / \".claude\" / \"state\"\n    ctx_file = state_dir / f\"ctx_{session}.json\"\n    band_file = state_dir / f\"ctx_{session}_band.json\"\n\n    try:\n        state = json.loads(ctx_file.read_text())\n        pct = float(state[\"pct\"])\n    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError):\n        return  # no status-line data yet: stay silent\n    try:\n        last_band = int(json.loads(band_file.read_text())[\"band\"])\n    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError):\n        last_band = NONE\n\n    log_usage(project, session, state)\n\n    msg, band = decide(pct, last_band)\n    try:\n        band_file.write_text(json.dumps({\"band\": band}))\n    except OSError:\n        pass\n    if msg:\n        print(json.dumps({\"systemMessage\": msg}))\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    try:\n        main()\n    except Exception:\n        pass  # a warning hook must never break the session\n {"parentUuid":"daf39e1d-d8cb-4553-aa49-81414ed0888f","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg4PGM9o8hK7SBqhLxy9L","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"记下了,之后不会再提截止日期。\n\n下一步是练习 A,也就是实现 `ctx_guard.py` 里的 `decide()`。我看了手册和测试,任务很小,10 个测试里有 7 个要靠这个函数通过。\n\n**练习 A 要在新会话里做,我不直接在这里写。** 手册要求先 `/clear`,再用 `/tdd` 驱动实现。评分项 B6 看的是会话纪律,而且 transcripts 要求一个会话一个文件。当前这个会话混了很多模型和套餐的讨论,在这里写会把这些都算进练习 A 的记录。请你在输入框里依次输入:\n\n```text\n/clear\n```\n```text\n/tdd Implement decide() in .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py so the failing tests in tests/test_ctx_guard.py pass. Do not change the tests or any other function.\n```\n\n新会话一开始,我会把 `exA` 写进 `.claude/state/phase`,用量记录就会按阶段标好。\n\n**收回我之前\"练习 A 和 B 并行\"的建议。** 我仔细看了钩子的实现,发现两个问题:\n- `.claude/state/phase` 和 `notes/usage-ledger.csv` 都按目录存放。两个窗口开在同一个目录,会共用一个 phase 文件,彼此的用量会被标错阶段。\n- 两个窗口如果用 Orca 各开一个 worktree,用量记录又会被拆成两份 CSV,合并时容易冲突。练习 B 和最后的报告都要读这份记录。\n\n练习 A 和 B 各自大约半小时,并行省下的时间不值得换来一份混乱的用量记录。按顺序做:A 完成后提交,`/clear`,再做 B。等到后面有互相独立的功能工单时,再考虑并行,到时我会先解决用量记录的问题。\n\n另外,WordPress 实地笔记(`notes/cms-field-notes.md`)需要你自己写,随时都可以做。"}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1298,"cache_read_input_tokens":88082,"output_tokens":1052,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":361},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1298,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1052,"cache_read_input_tokens":88082,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1298,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1298},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg4PGLmidKWpy8exj2CEo","type":"assistant","uuid":"b47356c5-382f-45c8-a68b-acecfc0eaaf6","timestamp":"2026-10-15T17:03:51.901Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"d0e77097-68d6-46af-9161-747ae084332c","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"9a7207af-4eee-48fb-8571-e2ec030ba9e2","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_011uw73uucAyFDTLvbXQuEXH","type":"tool_result","content":"225\t## Part 2 — See a real CMS before you design one\n226\t\n227\t**Time: 30 min. Usage cost: ~5%.**\n228\t\n229\tYou cannot be interviewed about something you have never used. Fix that first.\n230\t\n231\t### 2.1 Field trip: WordPress Playground\n232\t\n233\tOpen **`https://playground.wordpress.net`**. It runs a complete WordPress in your browser tab. Nothing installs; closing the tab wipes it. Break whatever you like.\n234\t\n235\tDo all six, in order:\n236\t\n237\t1. Write a **post**: title, a paragraph, **Save draft**. Visit the public site in another tab — it is not there.\n238\t2. **Publish** it. Reload the public site — now it is.\n239\t3. Write a **page** (\"About\"). Notice where pages show up that posts do not: the navigation menu.\n240\t4. Open **Settings → Permalinks**. Look at how the URL is built from the title. That string is the *slug*.\n241\t5. **Users → Add New**: create a user with the **Editor** role. Log out, log in as them. Try to reach **Users**. Write down exactly what happens.\n242\t6. Find where **Posts → All Posts** lets you filter by status. That screen is the content list you will build.\n243\t\n244\t### 2.2 Write your field notes\n245\t\n246\tCreate `notes/cms-field-notes.md` with **at least five** observations *in your own words*. Useful things to notice: what surprised you, what was hidden, what took more clicks than you expected, what you could not find, what an editor could not do.\n247\t\n248\tThese notes are graded (S1.1) and they are the raw material for your grill answers. Write like you are telling a friend, not like you are writing a lab report.\n249\t\n250\t### 2.3 Get the vocabulary\n251\t\n252\t```text\n253\t/clear\n254\t/research how content management systems model content, users and roles, and publishing — compare WordPress, Drupal, and static-site generators\n255\t```\n256\t\n257\tSkim the output for terms: *content type, slug, draft/published, role, capability, permalink, taxonomy, theme, headless*. You do not need all of them. You need the handful you will actually use.\n258\t\n259\t---\n260\t\n261\t## Part 3 — Your client\n262\t\n263\t**Time: 20 min.**\n264\t\n265\tYou are not building \"a CMS\". You are building one for someone, because specific people make specific demands, and those demands are what make your project yours.\n266\t\n267\t### 3.1 Pick a client\n268\t\n269\tChoose a real or plausible one you know something about: a club you belong to, a lab, a band, a campus office, a family business, a team. You will not contact them; you just need their reality.\n270\t\n271\t**If nothing comes to mind**, use the default:\n272\t\n273\t> **Knox County Historical Society.** Three volunteers run the site. Karen, the secretary, posts meeting announcements and event notices weekly; she is comfortable with email and nothing more. Tom, the president, writes longer research pieces every month or two and wants them to look permanent. Nobody should be able to edit the membership page except Tom. Their current site is a Facebook page they cannot search, and members ask them the same three questions every month: when is the next meeting, where is it, and what is on the agenda.\n274\t\n275\tIf you take the default, add **at least three details of your own** — a person, a constraint, a recurring frustration. Generic input produces a generic project, and that costs points under factor A.\n276\t\n277\t### 3.2 Write the brief\n278\t\n279\tCreate `notes/client-brief.md`. Half a page, in your words:\n280\t\n281\t- Who runs the site, and how comfortable are they with computers?\n282\t- Who reads it, and what are they usually trying to find?\n283\t- What is broken about how they do it now?\n284\t- What would make them say \"this is better\"?\n285\t- What must **not** happen? (e.g. \"a volunteer must never be able to delete the members page\")\n286\t\n287\t### 3.3 The required capabilities\n288\t\n289\tYour CMS can name things however your client would. Underneath, all seven of these must work. This list is fixed; how you get there is yours.\n290\t\n291\t1. **Login** — admins and editors sign in and out; passwords are stored hashed, never as text.\n292\t2. **Two roles** — *admin* and *editor*, with genuinely different permissions.\n293\t3. **Posts** — create, read, update, delete; title, slug, Markdown body, draft/published, author, timestamps.\n294\t4. **Pages** — same, and published pages appear in the public navigation.\n295\t5. **Admin console** — dashboard with counts, a content list you can filter, an editor with a preview.\n296\t6. **User management** — admin only: create users, change roles, deactivate; a deactivated user cannot log in.\n297\t7. **Public site and publish** — only published content, Markdown sanitized, nav built from pages, `cms publish` writes `site/` with relative paths.\n298\t\n299\t**Deliberately excluded** (do not build these): multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, rich-text WYSIWYG editors. They cost far more than they teach.\n300\t\n301\t---\n302\t"}]},"uuid":"e086a978-831e-4ea2-9418-aaf6ad064f07","timestamp":"2026-10-15T17:05:37.093Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md","content":"## Part 2 — See a real CMS before you design one\n\n**Time: 30 min. Usage cost: ~5%.**\n\nYou cannot be interviewed about something you have never used. Fix that first.\n\n### 2.1 Field trip: WordPress Playground\n\nOpen **`https://playground.wordpress.net`**. It runs a complete WordPress in your browser tab. Nothing installs; closing the tab wipes it. Break whatever you like.\n\nDo all six, in order:\n\n1. Write a **post**: title, a paragraph, **Save draft**. Visit the public site in another tab — it is not there.\n2. **Publish** it. Reload the public site — now it is.\n3. Write a **page** (\"About\"). Notice where pages show up that posts do not: the navigation menu.\n4. Open **Settings → Permalinks**. Look at how the URL is built from the title. That string is the *slug*.\n5. **Users → Add New**: create a user with the **Editor** role. Log out, log in as them. Try to reach **Users**. Write down exactly what happens.\n6. Find where **Posts → All Posts** lets you filter by status. That screen is the content list you will build.\n\n### 2.2 Write your field notes\n\nCreate `notes/cms-field-notes.md` with **at least five** observations *in your own words*. Useful things to notice: what surprised you, what was hidden, what took more clicks than you expected, what you could not find, what an editor could not do.\n\nThese notes are graded (S1.1) and they are the raw material for your grill answers. Write like you are telling a friend, not like you are writing a lab report.\n\n### 2.3 Get the vocabulary\n\n```text\n/clear\n/research how content management systems model content, users and roles, and publishing — compare WordPress, Drupal, and static-site generators\n```\n\nSkim the output for terms: *content type, slug, draft/published, role, capability, permalink, taxonomy, theme, headless*. You do not need all of them. You need the handful you will actually use.\n\n---\n\n## Part 3 — Your client\n\n**Time: 20 min.**\n\nYou are not building \"a CMS\". You are building one for someone, because specific people make specific demands, and those demands are what make your project yours.\n\n### 3.1 Pick a client\n\nChoose a real or plausible one you know something about: a club you belong to, a lab, a band, a campus office, a family business, a team. You will not contact them; you just need their reality.\n\n**If nothing comes to mind**, use the default:\n\n> **Knox County Historical Society.** Three volunteers run the site. Karen, the secretary, posts meeting announcements and event notices weekly; she is comfortable with email and nothing more. Tom, the president, writes longer research pieces every month or two and wants them to look permanent. Nobody should be able to edit the membership page except Tom. Their current site is a Facebook page they cannot search, and members ask them the same three questions every month: when is the next meeting, where is it, and what is on the agenda.\n\nIf you take the default, add **at least three details of your own** — a person, a constraint, a recurring frustration. Generic input produces a generic project, and that costs points under factor A.\n\n### 3.2 Write the brief\n\nCreate `notes/client-brief.md`. Half a page, in your words:\n\n- Who runs the site, and how comfortable are they with computers?\n- Who reads it, and what are they usually trying to find?\n- What is broken about how they do it now?\n- What would make them say \"this is better\"?\n- What must **not** happen? (e.g. \"a volunteer must never be able to delete the members page\")\n\n### 3.3 The required capabilities\n\nYour CMS can name things however your client would. Underneath, all seven of these must work. This list is fixed; how you get there is yours.\n\n1. **Login** — admins and editors sign in and out; passwords are stored hashed, never as text.\n2. **Two roles** — *admin* and *editor*, with genuinely different permissions.\n3. **Posts** — create, read, update, delete; title, slug, Markdown body, draft/published, author, timestamps.\n4. **Pages** — same, and published pages appear in the public navigation.\n5. **Admin console** — dashboard with counts, a content list you can filter, an editor with a preview.\n6. **User management** — admin only: create users, change roles, deactivate; a deactivated user cannot log in.\n7. **Public site and publish** — only published content, Markdown sanitized, nav built from pages, `cms publish` writes `site/` with relative paths.\n\n**Deliberately excluded** (do not build these): multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, rich-text WYSIWYG editors. They cost far more than they teach.\n\n---\n","numLines":78,"startLine":225,"totalLines":696}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"d0e77097-68d6-46af-9161-747ae084332c","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"f97047ce-5dd1-44c0-9190-0c48bb4de664","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg4PREJmzapo6m8CaBU4f","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"我上一条说得太简略了。分三点讲清楚。\n\n## 1. 要不要开新窗口\n\n不用另开窗口。手册说的\"新会话\"是指**清空上下文**,在当前窗口输入 `/clear` 就够了。`/clear` 之后,我会忘掉之前所有的对话,从头开始,效果和开一个新窗口一样。\n\n我之前不建议你同时开好几个窗口并行干活,但一个窗口里做完一件事、`/clear`、再做下一件,正是课程要求的做法。\n\n## 2. 现在要做什么\n\n按手册的顺序,还剩这些步骤。标\"你\"的必须你本人做,我不能代写:\n\n| 顺序 | 内容 | 谁做 | 大约时间 |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | **Part 2:去 WordPress Playground 操作一遍,写 field notes** | 你 | 30 分钟 |\n| 2 | Part 2.3:`/research` 查 CMS 相关术语 | 我 | 几分钟 |\n| 3 | **Part 3:选一个客户,写 `notes/client-brief.md`** | 你 | 20 分钟 |\n| 4 | Part 4:练习 A(`decide()`) | 我,用 `/tdd` | 30 分钟 |\n| 5 | Part 5:练习 B(`spend()`)和预算计划 | 我写代码,预算估计你来定 | 45 分钟 |\n| 6 | Part 6:grill → spec → tickets → 开始写功能 | 我们一起 | 主体工作 |\n\n建议先做第 1 项。原因是 grill 阶段我会一个问题一个问题地问你客户的需求,评分项 A1 专门看你的回答里有没有你自己的信息。field notes 和客户简介就是你回答问题的素材,没有它们,grill 就答不出东西。练习 A 和 B 跟这些无关,放在第 4、5 项任何时候做都行。\n\n## 3. field notes 要写成什么样\n\n**先做操作。** 打开 https://playground.wordpress.net,它会在浏览器里跑一个完整的 WordPress,不用安装。按顺序做这 6 件事:\n\n1. 写一篇 **post**,填标题和一段正文,点 **Save draft**。在另一个标签页打开公开网站,确认它**看不到**这篇草稿。\n2. 点 **Publish** 发布,刷新公开网站,确认现在能看到了。\n3. 写一个 **page**(比如 \"About\"),留意它出现在哪里,post 不会出现在那里,比如导航菜单。\n4. 打开 **Settings → Permalinks**,看网址是怎么从标题生成的,那串字就是 *slug*。\n5. **Users → Add New**,建一个 **Editor** 角色的用户。退出登录,用这个用户登录,再试着进入 **Users** 页面,**记下到底发生了什么**。\n6. 找到 **Posts → All Posts** 里按状态筛选的地方,你之后要做的内容列表就是这个页面。\n\n**评分要求**(S1.1,1 分):\n- 至少 **5 条**观察,用**你自己的话**写。\n- 手册原话是\"像跟朋友讲,不要像写实验报告\"。\n\n**可以写的方向:** 让你意外的地方、被藏起来找了半天的东西、比预想多点了几下的操作、找不到的功能、Editor 做不了的事。\n\n**要避开的写法**(评分标准里列为 AI 痕迹):每条长度都一样、到处都是三项并列、结尾再总结一遍开头、\"seamless\" 这类空话。\n\n**加分的写法**(评分标准里的人类写作特征):具体细节、吐槽或玩笑、承认自己卡住或搞错的地方、句子长短不一。\n\n**一个文件骨架,内容你来填:**\n\n```markdown\n# Field notes — WordPress Playground, 2026-10-xx\n\n1. 草稿 vs 发布:\n2. Page 和 Post 的区别:\n3. Slug / permalink:\n4. 用 Editor 登录后去 Users 页面:(写下你看到的原话或现象)\n5. 内容列表按状态筛选:\n6. (可选)其他让你意外的:\n```\n\n不一定要按这 6 个标题写,你也可以只写印象最深的 5 件事。\n\n**再提醒一点:** 评分项 A2 看 field notes 和 `CONTEXT.md` 有没有围绕一个具体的客户。你可以先想想第 3 部分要选谁,写笔记时顺手联系一下,比如\"如果是我的社团,谁会需要 Editor 权限\"。客户可以是你熟悉的社团、实验室或乐队。没有合适的,也可以用手册给的默认客户 Knox County Historical Society,但必须加上至少 3 个你自己编的细节。\n\n你写完后贴给我或者告诉我写好了,我可以检查条数和格式够不够,但不会改你的措辞。"}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4131,"cache_read_input_tokens":90514,"output_tokens":2161,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":462},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":4131,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2161,"cache_read_input_tokens":90514,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4131,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":4131},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg4PRE1fijA2pnDdXcTNH","type":"assistant","uuid":"42ae8894-de22-4324-80f9-c7c48599d692","timestamp":"2026-10-15T17:06:04.347Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"0f689b2b-09de-40a4-be3a-a420d2feb385","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"31381154-4f83-4e24-a281-26fcf3f350d7","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"\n\n<pasted_content id=\"a222\">\n第一个是发post的时候的高级setting里面有一个额外CSS，不能用自然语言，只能用color:red这种特殊形式\n\n编辑和快速编辑的区别，虽然不知道快速编辑为什么存在。\n\n有很多预设的配色方案 每个还有自己的名字 一个主题有四个配色，其中第四个配色不知道是分管哪里的\n\n用户发言需要审核，这个应该可以设置，但是我一开始没有注意到，管理员的功能有很多，但是索引不是很好，虽然可以搜索，但是有的功能很隐蔽，需要点好几次才能找到\n\n可以自定义网站链接，这一点我没想到，看起来好像只要前面是wordpress.net, /后面放什么都可以\n\n可以设置违禁关键字，但是是一个巨大的输入框，不知道具体怎么操作，词与词之间如何间隔\n\n可以为没有头像的用户自生成头像，不知道具体是怎么随机的\n\n底下有一个商店选项，但是没有任何指向页面，我记得上一次的时候还可以找到设置付费的页面，比如可以自定义优惠券，但是这次这个功能没有了\n\n我目前就看到了这些，我不知道是不是需要写这种，符合要求吗？\n\n</pasted_content id=\"a222\">\n"},"uuid":"dc3df878-09be-4184-83ed-6b7c353562da","timestamp":"2026-10-15T21:57:41.061Z","permissionMode":"bypassPermissions","origin":{"kind":"human"},"promptSource":"typed","turnOrigin":"human","turnPosition":{"promptIndex":14,"turnIndex":15},"userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

Field notes — WordPress Playground, 2026-10-15\n\n1. 第一个是发post的时候的高级setting里面有一个额外CSS，不能用自然语言，只能用color:red这种特殊形式\n\n2. 编辑和快速编辑的区别，虽然不知道快速编辑为什么存在。\n\n3. 有很多预设的配色方案 每个还有自己的名字 一个主题有四个配色，其中第四个配色不知道是分管哪里的\n\n4. 用户发言需要审核，这个应该可以设置，但是我一开始没有注意到，管理员的功能有很多，但是索引不是很好，虽然可以搜索，但是有的功能很隐蔽，需要点好几次才能找到\n\n5. 可以自定义网站链接，这一点我没想到，看起来好像只要前面是wordpress.net, /后面放什么都可以\n\n6. 可以设置违禁关键字，但是是一个巨大的输入框，不知道具体怎么操作，词与词之间如何间隔\n\n7. 可以为没有头像的用户自生成头像，不知道具体是怎么随机的\n\n8. 底下有一个商店选项，但是没有任何指向页面，我记得上一次的时候还可以找到设置付费的页面，比如可以自定义优惠券，但是这次这个功能没有了\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":74091,"cache_read_input_tokens":23193,"output_tokens":1570,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":531},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":74091,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1570,"cache_read_input_tokens":23193,"cache_creation_input_tokens":74091,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":74091},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":{"cache_miss_reason":{"type":"previous_message_not_found"}},"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_018fb9UERKQcEHWaj3KYjEk4":{"file_path":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/notes/cms-field-notes.md","content":"# Field notes — WordPress Playground, 2026-10-15\n\n1. 第一个是发post的时候的高级setting里面有一个额外CSS，不能用自然语言，只能用color:red这种特殊形式\n\n2. 编辑和快速编辑的区别，虽然不知道快速编辑为什么存在。\n\n3. 有很多预设的配色方案 每个还有自己的名字 一个主题有四个配色，其中第四个配色不知道是分管哪里的\n\n4. 用户发言需要审核，这个应该可以设置，但是我一开始没有注意到，管理员的功能有很多，但是索引不是很好，虽然可以搜索，但是有的功能很隐蔽，需要点好几次才能找到\n\n5. 可以自定义网站链接，这一点我没想到，看起来好像只要前面是wordpress.net, /后面放什么都可以\n\n6. 可以设置违禁关键字，但是是一个巨大的输入框，不知道具体怎么操作，词与词之间如何间隔\n\n7. 可以为没有头像的用户自生成头像，不知道具体是怎么随机的\n\n8. 底下有一个商店选项，但是没有任何指向页面，我记得上一次的时候还可以找到设置付费的页面，比如可以自定义优惠券，但是这次这个功能没有了\n"}},"apiBlockIndex":2,"requestId":"req_011Cg4mgvA96H6dxh7Bwcm4u","type":"assistant","uuid":"cf69fb34-5d81-4bca-a4e8-984ea5b4db2f","timestamp":"2026-10-15T21:58:02.367Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"3aab11d0-7d02-46cc-9cb1-c2f90b89e98c","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg4n8e9Cf3TwEcHjnjnRa","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"先回答你最关心的语言问题,再说这几条新观察。\n\n## 提交物要用英文吗\n\n是的,建议全部用英文。评分标准和手册都没有明确规定语言,我查过了。但这是 Kenyon 的英文课程,教授和评分系统默认读英文,交一堆中文确实不合适,你的判断是对的。\n\n**难点在于 \"in your own words\"。** field notes(S1.1)、grill 里你的回答(A1)、commit 信息和 review 回复(A5)、报告(A3)都要求是你自己写的。如果你用中文写、我翻成英文,那就成了 AI 写的英文,很可能带上评分标准列的 AI 痕迹,而且严格说已经不算\"你自己的话\"。\n\n**我建议这样分工:**\n- **你本人写的部分用英文写,写得粗糙没关系**,包括 field notes、客户简介、grill 里的回答、报告。语法不完美、句子短,反而更像真人,评分标准把句子长短不一列为加分特征。\n- **你可以先用中文想清楚,自己写英文。** 卡住的词问我,比如\"审核用哪个词\",我只告诉你那个词,不替你写整句。\n- **我生成的东西本来就是英文**,包括代码、`CONTEXT.md`、spec、tickets、ADR,这部分不用担心。\n- 和我对话用中文完全没问题。只是 grill 的记录会被抽查 10 条回答,所以 grill 那一轮请尽量用英文回答。\n\n那 8 条中文笔记我先留在文件里,等你英文版写好再替换,不会以中文提交。\n\n## 新观察,有两处要确认\n\n**1. 草稿和发布:** 你写的是\"发布之后需要管理员审核才能看到\",后面又说\"如果用户之前有通过审核的评论,新评论就不用审核\"。这两件事我觉得可能混在一起了:\n- WordPress 里,管理员发布的 **post** 通常会立刻出现在公开网站上,不需要审核。\n- 需要审核的一般是访客留的**评论**,你后半句说的就是评论审核的设置。\n\n你回想一下:点 Publish 之后刷新公开网站,**那篇文章本身**能看到吗?这正好对应你 CMS 的核心规则,也就是 `CLAUDE.md` 里写的\"只有已发布的内容才能出现在网站上\",所以值得弄清楚。\n\n**2. Editor 权限:** 你写的是管理员能删除用户、发重置密码链接,这是从管理员角度看的。手册第 5 步要的是反过来:**退出登录,用新建的 Editor 账号登录,再试着打开 Users 页面**,看会发生什么。这是你 CMS 里 admin 和 editor 最关键的区别,grill 时我一定会问,建议你回去做一下这一步。\n\n**3. Google 提示密码泄露:** 这个观察很好,建议保留。我比较确定原因:Google 密码管理器会把你保存的密码和公开的泄露数据库比对,这个密码出现在已知泄露列表里就会报警。所以几乎可以肯定是你设的密码太常见(比如 `password123` 这类),不是 WordPress 泄露了你的数据。Playground 只在你的浏览器里运行,数据不会上传。这条正好和项目要求呼应:`CLAUDE.md` 规定密码必须用 argon2 哈希存储,grill 时也可以讨论要不要拒绝常见弱密码。\n\n你英文版写好、或者确认完上面两处后发给我,我来更新文件。"}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1202,"cache_read_input_tokens":99489,"output_tokens":1247,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":22},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1202,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1247,"cache_read_input_tokens":99489,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1202,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1202},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg4n8dsanretUWv9BcfR6","type":"assistant","uuid":"9c1a4ff8-1f66-4434-9db0-35b49ffe2800","timestamp":"2026-10-15T22:03:48.392Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"56dfe560-4064-47f2-b250-fbc73759f74f","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg4nmbvH1bz8jqmvcJMu9","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"这样就都清楚了,两条都是有用的观察:\n- **发布后立刻可见**:草稿看不到,发布后马上能看到。前面说的审核只针对评论。\n- **Editor 登录后根本没有 Users 菜单**:只有 admin 才有。\n\n关于第二条,有一个值得多花一分钟的小实验。用 Editor 登录后,直接在地址栏输入 Users 页面的网址,也就是把网址末尾改成 `/wp-admin/users.php`,看会发生什么。\n\n这能区分两件事:WordPress 只是**把菜单藏起来了**,还是**真的禁止了访问**。手册第 0 部分有一句话:\"权限要么在代码里强制执行,要么就不是真的。\" 只藏菜单不算权限控制,知道网址的人照样能进去。你自己的 CMS 也会碰到这个问题,所以 grill 时这是很好的素材。\n\n## 现在你有的全部观察\n\n写英文版时可以对照这张清单,不用全写,挑 5 条以上即可:\n\n1. 额外 CSS 只能写代码,不能用自然语言\n2. 编辑和快速编辑,不知道快速编辑为什么存在\n3. 主题有 4 个配色,第 4 个不知道管哪里\n4. 评论要审核(之前审核通过的人可以免审);后台功能多,但很难找\n5. 可以自定义链接,也就是 slug\n6. 违禁词是一个巨大的输入框,不知道词之间怎么分隔\n7. 自动生成头像,不知道怎么随机\n8. 商店选项点了没反应,上次还能设置优惠券\n9. 草稿在公开网站看不到,发布后立刻能看到\n10. Page 会出现在导航菜单里,post 不会\n11. Editor 登录后完全没有 Users 菜单,只有 admin 有(地址栏实验的结果可以加在这里)\n12. 新建用户时 Google 提示这组账号密码已泄露\n\n**建议优先写 9、10、11、12。** 它们直接对应你要做的功能:发布、页面导航、角色权限、密码安全。\n\n用英文写,一条一两句就够,像跟朋友讲那样。写的时候有不会的词随时问我,比如\"审核\"或\"快速编辑\"在英文界面里叫什么,我只告诉你那个词。写完贴过来,我替换掉文件里的中文版本。"}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1315,"cache_read_input_tokens":100691,"output_tokens":1062,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":241},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1315,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1062,"cache_read_input_tokens":100691,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1315,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1315},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg4nmawFpHEBwV5hEyCvG","type":"assistant","uuid":"79fe8abd-3196-4d4f-9d83-d904cfd0df04","timestamp":"2026-10-15T22:12:14.377Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"5d67ba0c-9e09-4710-bb80-4cc45254429c","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg4oLxMGaPd5eo1zAg1GK","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01VePBuTeBTeF4DR3oqDdvMk","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/notes/cms-field-notes.md","content":"# Field notes — WordPress Playground, 2026-10-15\n\n1. When I wrote a post, the advanced settings had an **Additional CSS** box. You can't type normal language there, only that special format like `color: red`.\n\n2. There's **Edit** and **Quick Edit**. I'm not sure why Quick Edit exists.\n\n3. There are a lot of preset color schemes and each one has its own name. A theme has four colors, and I couldn't figure out what the fourth one controls.\n\n4. Comments need approval before they show up. You can change this, but I didn't notice it at first. Right now it's set so that if someone already has an approved comment, their new comments skip approval. In general the admin side has tons of features but they're badly organized. There is a search, but some features are hidden and take several clicks to find.\n\n5. You can set your own link for a page (the **slug**, under **Permalinks**). I didn't expect that. It looks like as long as the front part is the site address, you can put almost anything after the `/`.\n\n6. You can set **Disallowed Comment Keys** (banned words), but it's just one giant text box. I didn't know how to use it or how to separate one word from the next.\n\n7. It can generate an avatar for users who don't have one (**Default Avatar**). I don't know how it decides what to generate.\n\n8. There's a **Shop** option near the bottom, but clicking it doesn't go anywhere. I remember last time I could find pages for paid stuff, like making custom coupons, but that's gone this time.\n\n9. A **draft** doesn't show up on the public site. Once I hit **Publish** it showed up right away.\n\n10. A **Page** (I made \"About\") shows up in the navigation menu. Posts don't.\n\n11. When I logged in as an **Editor**, the **Users** menu was just gone. Only the admin has it. I also tried typing the Users page URL directly as the editor, and I couldn't get to it at all.\n\n12. I made a new user and saved the username and password in my browser. Google immediately told me this username/password combo had been leaked. I don't know exactly why.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":105,"cache_read_input_tokens":103068,"output_tokens":1737,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":839},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":105,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1737,"cache_read_input_tokens":103068,"cache_creation_input_tokens":105,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":105},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01VePBuTeBTeF4DR3oqDdvMk":{"file_path":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/notes/cms-field-notes.md","content":"# Field notes — WordPress Playground, 2026-10-15\n\n1. When I wrote a post, the advanced settings had an **Additional CSS** box. You can't type normal language there, only that special format like `color: red`.\n\n2. There's **Edit** and **Quick Edit**. I'm not sure why Quick Edit exists.\n\n3. There are a lot of preset color schemes and each one has its own name. A theme has four colors, and I couldn't figure out what the fourth one controls.\n\n4. Comments need approval before they show up. You can change this, but I didn't notice it at first. Right now it's set so that if someone already has an approved comment, their new comments skip approval. In general the admin side has tons of features but they're badly organized. There is a search, but some features are hidden and take several clicks to find.\n\n5. You can set your own link for a page (the **slug**, under **Permalinks**). I didn't expect that. It looks like as long as the front part is the site address, you can put almost anything after the `/`.\n\n6. You can set **Disallowed Comment Keys** (banned words), but it's just one giant text box. I didn't know how to use it or how to separate one word from the next.\n\n7. It can generate an avatar for users who don't have one (**Default Avatar**). I don't know how it decides what to generate.\n\n8. There's a **Shop** option near the bottom, but clicking it doesn't go anywhere. I remember last time I could find pages for paid stuff, like making custom coupons, but that's gone this time.\n\n9. A **draft** doesn't show up on the public site. Once I hit **Publish** it showed up right away.\n\n10. A **Page** (I made \"About\") shows up in the navigation menu. Posts don't.\n\n11. When I logged in as an **Editor**, the **Users** menu was just gone. Only the admin has it. I also tried typing the Users page URL directly as the editor, and I couldn't get to it at all.\n\n12. I made a new user and saved the username and password in my browser. Google immediately told me this username/password combo had been leaked. I don't know exactly why.\n"}},"apiBlockIndex":2,"requestId":"req_011Cg4oLwwECbUmNrUEnEq9i","type":"assistant","uuid":"cee9f274-47b0-4abc-8134-9ddf0f32cc9e","timestamp":"2026-10-15T22:19:42.724Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

When I was writing new posts, the advanced settings had a box called additional CSS. I tried to type some words there, but it only accept specific format input, such as “color: red”\n\n2. the admin account can both edit and quick edit each post. I don’t quite understand why the quick edit function is necessary, is it for the convinence of the admin?\n\n3. There are some preset color schemes with their names. Each theme has four colors, but I did not find what the fourth color controls.\n\n4. I made a comment with a subscriber account and it did not appear until I approved it using the admin account. Then I noticed that there were two options — one is that every comments need approval, and the other is that once an user have previously approved comments, their future comments will not need approval to appear. Generally, the admin account has a lot of features and it is kind of diffcult to quickly locate the wanted feature every time.\n\n5. I did not expect that I can set my own link for the webpage. It looks like as long as the front part is the web address, and after the “/”, the rest part can be anything.\n\n6. There is a box that the admin account can put some words to ban them from comments. It is just one text box, so I am not sure if I want to put several different word or phrases in it, how I could separate them .\n\n7. There is a shop option near the bottom, but it does not redirect to anywhere when clicking. When last time I navigate, I remember that I can adjust this function at the setting part, such as make custom coupons, but this time it disappear.\n\n8. The draft does not show up on public site. When I was writing new posts, the advanced settings had a box called additional CSS. I tried to type some words there, but it only accept specific format input, such as “color: red”\n\n2. the admin account can both edit and quick edit each post. I don’t quite understand why the quick edit function is necessary, is it for the convinence of the admin?\n\n3. There are some preset color schemes with their names. Each theme has four colors, but I did not find what the fourth color controls.\n\n4. I made a comment with a subscriber account and it did not appear until I approved it using the admin account. Then I noticed that there were two options — one is that every comments need approval, and the other is that once an user have previously approved comments, their future comments will not need approval to appear. Generally, the admin account has a lot of features and it is kind of diffcult to quickly locate the wanted feature every time.\n\n5. I did not expect that I can set my own link for the webpage. It looks like as long as the front part is the web address, and after the “/”, the rest part can be anything.\n\n6. There is a box that the admin account can put some words to ban them from comments. It is just one text box, so I am not sure if I want to put several different word or phrases in it, how I could separate them .\n\n7. There is a shop option near the bottom, but it does not redirect to anywhere when clicking. When last time I navigate, I remember that I can adjust this function at the setting part, such as make custom coupons, but this time it disappear.\n\n8. The draft does not show up on public site. It only appears after publishing.\n\n9. Only admin account has the users menu and editor does not. I also tried typing the URL directly as the aditor, but that also does not work.\n\n10. I created several accounts and saved the username and password in chrome. I tried to type some words there, but it only accept specific format input, such as “color: red”\n4\t\n5\t2. the admin account can both edit and quick edit each post. I don’t quite understand why the quick edit function is necessary, is it for the convenience of the admin?\n6\t\n7\t3. There are some preset color schemes with their names. Each theme has four colors, but I did not find what the fourth color controls.\n8\t\n9\t4. I made a comment with a subscriber account and it did not appear until I approved it using the admin account. Then I noticed that there were two options — one is that every comments need approval, and the other is that once an user have previously approved comments, their future comments will not need approval to appear. Generally, the admin account has a lot of features and it is kind of difficult to quickly locate the wanted feature every time.\n10\t\n11\t5. I did not expect that I can set my own link for the webpage. It looks like as long as the front part is the web address, and after the “/”, the rest part can be anything.\n12\t\n13\t6. There is a box that the admin account can put some words to ban them from comments. It is just one text box, so I am not sure if I want to put several different word or phrases in it, how I could separate them .\n14\t\n15\t7. There is a shop option near the bottom, but it does not redirect to anywhere when clicking. When last time I navigate, I remember that I can adjust this function at the setting part, such as make custom coupons, but this time it disappear.\n16\t\n17\t8. The draft does not show up on public site. It only appears after publishing.\n18\t\n19\t9. Only admin account has the users menu and editor does not. I also tried typing the URL directly as the editor, but that also does not work.\n20\t\n21\t10. I created several accounts and saved the username and password in chrome. I don’t quite understand why the quick edit function is necessary, is it for the convenience of the admin?\n6\t\n7\t3. There are some preset color schemes with their names. Generally, the admin account has a lot of features and it is kind of difficult to quickly locate the wanted feature every time.\n10\t\n11\t5. There is a box that the admin account can put some words to ban them from comments. {"parentUuid":"a753b34c-d541-48f2-aab1-806862630aab","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg4tyEagJ42WiYob76Mss","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"三处拼写都改好了:`convenience`、`difficult`、`the editor`。grep 那一步报的退出码 1,是因为确认旧拼写已经不存在时匹配数为 0,不是出错。语法上的小问题(比如 `an user`、`every comments`)我没动,你只说了改拼写。\n\n## 这个项目要做什么\n\n**一句话:** 给一个具体的组织做一个小型网站管理系统(CMS),让不懂技术的人也能写文章、发布到网上。\n\n**它分成两半:**\n\n```\n你的电脑(私有)                              公开网络\n┌──────────────────────────┐\n│ 管理后台(网页界面)        │\n│  登录 → 写文章/页面 → 存草稿 │\n│        ↓                 │\n│   数据库(SQLite)          │\n│        ↓                 │\n│ cms publish 命令          │ ──→ 静态网页 ──→ GitHub Pages(所有人可见)\n└──────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n- **管理后台**只在你自己电脑上运行,相当于 WordPress 的 wp-admin。\n- **公开网站**是导出的纯 HTML 网页,放在 GitHub Pages 上。上面只有已发布的内容,草稿永远不会出现。\n- 你在 WordPress 里看到的几件事,正是你要自己做出来的:草稿和发布的区别、Editor 看不到 Users 菜单、Page 出现在导航里。\n\n**必须实现的 7 项功能**(手册写死的,名字可以按你客户的习惯叫):\n\n| # | 功能 | 你在 WordPress 里见过的对应 |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | 登录:admin 和 editor 能登录登出,密码哈希存储 | 登录页 |\n| 2 | 两种角色:admin 和 editor 权限真的不同 | Editor 没有 Users 菜单 |\n| 3 | 文章(posts):增删改查,有标题、slug、Markdown 正文、草稿/发布、作者、时间 | Posts |\n| 4 | 页面(pages):同上,已发布的页面出现在公开网站的导航里 | Pages,比如 About |\n| 5 | 管理后台:有统计数字的首页、可筛选的内容列表、带预览的编辑器 | Dashboard、All Posts 筛选 |\n| 6 | 用户管理(只有 admin):建用户、改角色、停用,停用的人不能登录 | Users |\n| 7 | 公开网站和发布:只导出已发布内容,Markdown 要过滤,导航由页面生成 | 公开网站 |\n\n**明确不用做的:** 多站点、拖拽式页面搭建器、所见即所得的富文本编辑器。\n\n## 客户是什么\n\n这里的\"客户\"(client)是**你假设在给谁做这个网站**,不是客服。你不用真的去联系对方,只要你了解他们的情况就行。\n\n**为什么这一步重要:**\n- 评分项 A2(3 分)看 field notes、`CONTEXT.md` 和网站内容是否围绕同一个具体客户,用的是不是这个客户的说法。\n- grill 阶段我会一直问\"你的客户需要什么\",评分项 A1(5 分)看你的回答里有没有自己补充的客户细节。你越了解这个客户,这两项越好拿分。\n\n**怎么选:** 挑一个你真正熟悉的组织,比如你参加的社团、你工作过的实验室或办公室、一个乐队、学生会、家里的生意、一支球队。关键是你知道里面**有哪些人、谁负责写东西、谁不该碰什么、现在哪里不方便**。\n\n想不出来也可以用手册给的默认客户:Knox County Historical Society,一个三名志愿者运营的历史学会。用这个的话必须**自己加至少 3 个细节**,否则会被判为\"太泛\",在 A2 上丢分。\n\n**举几个例子帮你想**,只是方向,不是推荐:\n- 你参加的某个学生社团:社长发活动通知,干事写活动回顾,只有社长能改\"关于我们\"页面。\n- 一个你帮过忙的实验室:导师发研究动态,研究生写论文摘要,成员名单页面只有导师能改。\n- 家里或朋友的小店:老板发新品和营业时间,店员写日常更新,不能让店员改价格页面。\n\n## 客户简介要写什么\n\n文件是 `notes/client-brief.md`,半页左右,用英文、用你自己的话,回答 5 个问题:\n\n1. **谁来管理网站?** 他们对电脑熟不熟?\n2. **谁来看网站?** 他们通常想找什么?\n3. **现在的做法哪里不好?** 比如只用微信群或 Instagram,信息找不到。\n4. **怎样会让他们觉得\"这样好多了\"?**\n5. **什么事绝对不能发生?** 比如\"普通成员绝不能删掉会员页面\"。\n\n第 5 条会直接变成你 CMS 的权限规则,所以要想具体一点。\n\n**接下来:** 你先决定选哪个客户,然后用中文把这 5 个问题的答案大概说给我听,想到什么说什么。我按你的意思出英文草稿,放到单独的文件里给你改,改完我再放进去,和 field notes 的流程一样。"}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1239,"cache_read_input_tokens":110060,"output_tokens":1955,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":136},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1239,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1955,"cache_read_input_tokens":110060,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1239,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1239},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg4tyEHZQPpwiS5QcLPys","type":"assistant","uuid":"779eff60-2075-4387-b9f9-c90f1e1f4b6f","timestamp":"2026-10-15T23:33:32.940Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"acc086d9-cc81-4a6b-8e67-249315c5be50","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"0e93f3d1-cd81-464e-98d6-1efb3e1109c5","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"我想给大巴扎中文社群做一个网页，不算是一个组织，但是群体很明显。现在的群体的大本营是bilibili,几个头部的主播以及他们的粉丝，主播会直播和发视频，粉丝看直播或者视频评论区评论。管理网站的人可以是那几个主播，因为他们相对有名，而且有管理粉丝群的经验，但是他们对电脑不熟。来看网站的就是任何玩这个游戏的人，因为这个游戏有很强的攻略属性，因为相对于moba,fps来说，卡牌游戏相对偏向策略性而非操作性，所以这也就使得攻略的需求会比其他游戏更大。现在用Bilibili的问题是视频或者直播不像文字攻略一样可以用碎片化时间或者不方便听声音的时候获取，而终局阵容这种比较明确的东西在视频中难以定位，现在up主的攻略做法都是对着ppt讲视频，这样还不如建立一个论坛式的网页（如旅法师营地）来提供一个渠道。现在他们还没有网页，我觉得网页最大的优点就在于信息的可获取性。绝对不能发生的事情从网页设计来说就像你说的普通成员和admin的权限应该大有不同。比如管理员应该可以操控整个用户以及post页面。普通成员应该只有发贴子和发评论的权利，管理员会希望审核内容，可以只审核贴子，评论可以相对放宽。暂时就想到这些，因为现在还不是最终设计阶段，所以目前就这些"},"uuid":"3d9c69d8-f46f-44de-a1b1-4b6e72336da6","timestamp":"2026-10-16T04:17:05.713Z","permissionMode":"bypassPermissions","origin":{"kind":"human"},"promptSource":"typed","turnOrigin":"human","turnPosition":{"promptIndex":21,"turnIndex":22},"userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"b9d5243e-2dfa-4c1b-8bc4-6148adfa3eae","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg5Gd1mF4Be3aDBBHq2g1","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01XM2GnwakG8jZWkfJwiMRRS","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf/scratchpad/client-brief-draft.md","content":"# Client brief — The Bazaar Chinese community\n\nThe client is the Chinese-speaking player community of **The Bazaar** (大巴扎). It is not a formal organization, but it is a clear group. Right now its home base is **Bilibili**: a few top streamers (**up主**) and their fans. The streamers do live streams and post videos. Fans watch the streams or videos and talk in the comment sections.\n\n## Who runs the site\n\nThe site would be run by those few top streamers. They are fairly well known and they already have experience managing fan groups. But they are not very comfortable with computers.\n\n## Who reads it, and what they want\n\nAnyone who plays the game. The Bazaar has a strong guide culture. Compared with MOBAs or FPS games, a card game is more about strategy than mechanics, so players need guides more than in other games.\n\n## What is broken right now\n\nEverything is on Bilibili, and it is all video or live streams. A video is not like a written guide: you can't read it in a few spare minutes, or when you can't turn the sound on. Clear-cut information like **end-game builds** (终局阵容) is hard to find inside a video. Right now most streamers make guides by talking over a PowerPoint. A forum-style website (like **旅法师营地**) would be a better channel for this.\n\n## What would make them say \"this is better\"\n\nThey don't have a website yet. The biggest advantage of a website is that the information is easy to get to.\n\n## What must not happen\n\nRegular members and admins must have very different permissions. Admins should be able to control all users and all post pages. Regular members should only be able to make posts and write comments. Admins want to review content: posts should be reviewed before they go up, but comments can be looser.\n\nThis is not the final design yet, so this is what I have for now.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":90667,"cache_read_input_tokens":23193,"output_tokens":1726,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":818},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":90667,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1726,"cache_read_input_tokens":23193,"cache_creation_input_tokens":90667,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":90667},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":{"cache_miss_reason":{"type":"previous_message_not_found"}},"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01XM2GnwakG8jZWkfJwiMRRS":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf/scratchpad/client-brief-draft.md","content":"# Client brief — The Bazaar Chinese community\n\nThe client is the Chinese-speaking player community of **The Bazaar** (大巴扎). It is not a formal organization, but it is a clear group. Right now its home base is **Bilibili**: a few top streamers (**up主**) and their fans. The streamers do live streams and post videos. Fans watch the streams or videos and talk in the comment sections.\n\n## Who runs the site\n\nThe site would be run by those few top streamers. They are fairly well known and they already have experience managing fan groups. But they are not very comfortable with computers.\n\n## Who reads it, and what they want\n\nAnyone who plays the game. The Bazaar has a strong guide culture. Compared with MOBAs or FPS games, a card game is more about strategy than mechanics, so players need guides more than in other games.\n\n## What is broken right now\n\nEverything is on Bilibili, and it is all video or live streams. A video is not like a written guide: you can't read it in a few spare minutes, or when you can't turn the sound on. Clear-cut information like **end-game builds** (终局阵容) is hard to find inside a video. Right now most streamers make guides by talking over a PowerPoint. A forum-style website (like **旅法师营地**) would be a better channel for this.\n\n## What would make them say \"this is better\"\n\nThey don't have a website yet. The biggest advantage of a website is that the information is easy to get to.\n\n## What must not happen\n\nRegular members and admins must have very different permissions. Admins should be able to control all users and all post pages. Regular members should only be able to make posts and write comments. Admins want to review content: posts should be reviewed before they go up, but comments can be looser.\n\nThis is not the final design yet, so this is what I have for now.\n"}},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg5GczysgMCZM4q3PSQZP","type":"assistant","uuid":"cc2d1d22-5203-4323-a6d5-15e4cb42d1ea","timestamp":"2026-10-16T04:17:23.862Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"2d87374c-1e70-40e1-847e-86752f8b0b11","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg5GeXNW1yPskN6ButYdH","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"英文草稿已经在 VS Code 里打开,文件是 scratchpad 里的 `client-brief-draft.md`。正式文件 `notes/client-brief.md` 还没创建。我按你说的意思直译,结构对应手册的 5 个问题,没有加你没说过的内容。专有名词用粗体标了:**The Bazaar**、**Bilibili**、**up主**、**end-game builds**、**旅法师营地**。\n\n这个客户选得好:具体,有明确的人群,而且你本人了解。\"攻略在视频里难定位\"是一个很真实的痛点,评分项 A2 会喜欢这种素材。\n\n**不过有一个和项目范围的冲突,你改之前要先知道。**\n\n你设想的是论坛式网站,普通成员能发帖、评论,管理员审核。但这个项目要做的 CMS 结构不支持这种用法:\n\n- **公开网站是纯静态网页**,导出后放在 GitHub Pages 上,只能看,不能登录、不能发帖、不能评论。\n- **只有管理后台能写内容**,而它只在你自己电脑上运行,不上网。所以\"粉丝来网站发帖\"在这个架构里做不到。\n- 手册规定的两个角色是 **admin** 和 **editor**,两者都是写内容的人,没有\"普通读者账号\"。\n\n**我建议把你的想法这样对应过来,意思基本不变:**\n\n| 你的设想 | 放进这个项目 |\n|---|---|\n| 管理员(头部主播) | **admin**:管理所有用户和所有内容 |\n| 普通成员发帖 | **editor**:被邀请的攻略作者,可以是其他 up 主或资深玩家,能写攻略,但不能管理用户 |\n| 管理员审核帖子 | editor 写的攻略先存成草稿,由 admin 审核后发布。这比必做功能多一点工作,grill 时可以决定做不做 |\n| 粉丝评论 | 不做,静态网站做不了。评论留在 Bilibili |\n| 来看网站的人 | 所有玩家,只读,不用登录 |\n\n这样\"网站最大的优点是信息好找\"这个核心卖点完全保留,比如终局阵容可以直接按英雄分类、用文字写清楚。\n\n**你可以选:**\n- **按上表调整**(我推荐):我照这个思路改写草稿里的\"谁管理网站\"和\"什么绝对不能发生\"两段,你再改。\n- **保持原样**:客户简介写的是客户想要什么,可以比最终做的多,砍范围的事留到 grill 和 spec 阶段。这样也说得通,只是 grill 时会花时间在这上面。\n\n**还有一个小建议:** 简介里如果写到具体主播,不要用真实的 B 站 ID。这个仓库是公开的,写真名会让人以为他们参与了这个项目。用 \"Streamer A\" 这类代称,或者编一个名字就行。\n\n你选哪种?或者你直接在草稿里改,改完告诉我。"}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1930,"cache_read_input_tokens":113860,"output_tokens":1044,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":13},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1930,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1044,"cache_read_input_tokens":113860,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1930,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1930},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg5GeX6djznJrWhhM7A33","type":"assistant","uuid":"f2229a1a-bfc6-48cf-8a02-cb69b6f324b0","timestamp":"2026-10-16T04:17:39.100Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"2022c7d9-22ef-40a6-8bfa-2c7f70589ae5","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"b4bc902a-9e6f-488d-a97e-5bf605f45c76","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_016CTiXBb24xFnXd4rzWiruA","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Client brief — The Bazaar Chinese community\n2\t\n3\tThe client is the Chinese-speaking player community of **The Bazaar** (大巴扎). It is not a formal organization, but it is a clear group. Right now its home base is **Bilibili**: a few top streamers (**up主**) and their fans. The streamers do live streams and post videos. Fans watch the streams or videos and talk in the comment sections.\n4\t\n5\t## Who runs the site\n6\t\n7\tThe site would be run by those few top streamers. They are fairly well known and they already have experience managing fan groups. But they are not very comfortable with computers.\n8\t\n9\t## Who reads it, and what they want\n10\t\n11\tAnyone who plays the game. The Bazaar has a strong guide culture. Compared with MOBAs or FPS games, a card game is more about strategy than mechanics, so players need guides more than in other games.\n12\t\n13\t## What is broken right now\n14\t\n15\tEverything is on Bilibili, and it is all video or live streams. A video is not like a written guide: you can't read it in a few spare minutes, or when you can't turn the sound on. Clear-cut information like **end-game builds** (终局阵容) is hard to find inside a video. Right now most streamers make guides by talking over a PowerPoint. A forum-style website (like **旅法师营地**) would be a better channel for this.\n16\t\n17\t## What would make them say \"this is better\"\n18\t\n19\tThey don't have a website yet. The biggest advantage of a website is that the information is easy to get to.\n20\t\n21\t## What must not happen\n22\t\n23\tRegular members and admins must have very different permissions. Admins should be able to control all users and all post pages. Regular members should only be able to make posts and write comments. Admins want to review content: posts should be reviewed before they go up, but comments can be looser.\n24\t\n25\tThis is not the final design yet, so this is what I have for now.\n26\t"}]},"uuid":"75d383f3-0ca1-4b22-89f7-9131dd73b419","timestamp":"2026-10-16T04:19:45.236Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf/scratchpad/client-brief-draft.md","content":"# Client brief — The Bazaar Chinese community\n\nThe client is the Chinese-speaking player community of **The Bazaar** (大巴扎). It is not a formal organization, but it is a clear group. Right now its home base is **Bilibili**: a few top streamers (**up主**) and their fans. The streamers do live streams and post videos. Fans watch the streams or videos and talk in the comment sections.\n\n## Who runs the site\n\nThe site would be run by those few top streamers. They are fairly well known and they already have experience managing fan groups. But they are not very comfortable with computers.\n\n## Who reads it, and what they want\n\nAnyone who plays the game. The Bazaar has a strong guide culture. Compared with MOBAs or FPS games, a card game is more about strategy than mechanics, so players need guides more than in other games.\n\n## What is broken right now\n\nEverything is on Bilibili, and it is all video or live streams. A video is not like a written guide: you can't read it in a few spare minutes, or when you can't turn the sound on. Clear-cut information like **end-game builds** (终局阵容) is hard to find inside a video. Right now most streamers make guides by talking over a PowerPoint. A forum-style website (like **旅法师营地**) would be a better channel for this.\n\n## What would make them say \"this is better\"\n\nThey don't have a website yet. The biggest advantage of a website is that the information is easy to get to.\n\n## What must not happen\n\nRegular members and admins must have very different permissions. Admins should be able to control all users and all post pages. Regular members should only be able to make posts and write comments. Admins want to review content: posts should be reviewed before they go up, but comments can be looser.\n\nThis is not the final design yet, so this is what I have for now.\n","numLines":26,"startLine":1,"totalLines":26}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"2022c7d9-22ef-40a6-8bfa-2c7f70589ae5","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

They can write guides, but they can't manage users.","originalFile":"# Client brief — The Bazaar Chinese community\n\nThe client is the Chinese-speaking player community of **The Bazaar** (大巴扎). It is not a formal organization, but it is a clear group. Right now its home base is **Bilibili**: a few top streamers (**up主**) and their fans. The streamers do live streams and post videos. Fans watch the streams or videos and talk in the comment sections.\n\n## Who runs the site\n\nThe site would be run by those few top streamers. They are fairly well known and they already have experience managing fan groups. But they are not very comfortable with computers.\n\n## Who reads it, and what they want\n\nAnyone who plays the game. The Bazaar has a strong guide culture. Compared with MOBAs or FPS games, a card game is more about strategy than mechanics, so players need guides more than in other games.\n\n## What is broken right now\n\nEverything is on Bilibili, and it is all video or live streams. A video is not like a written guide: you can't read it in a few spare minutes, or when you can't turn the sound on. Clear-cut information like **end-game builds** (终局阵容) is hard to find inside a video. Right now most streamers make guides by talking over a PowerPoint. A forum-style website (like **旅法师营地**) would be a better channel for this.\n\n## What would make them say \"this is better\"\n\nThey don't have a website yet. The biggest advantage of a website is that the information is easy to get to.\n\n## What must not happen\n\nRegular members and admins must have very different permissions. Admins should be able to control all users and all post pages. Regular members should only be able to make posts and write comments. Admins want to review content: posts should be reviewed before they go up, but comments can be looser.\n\nThis is not the final design yet, so this is what I have for now.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":4,"oldLines":8,"newStart":4,"newLines":10,"lines":[" "," ## Who runs the site"," ","-The site would be run by those few top streamers. Comments and discussion can stay on Bilibili.","originalFile":"# Client brief — The Bazaar Chinese community\n\nThe client is the Chinese-speaking player community of **The Bazaar** (大巴扎). It is not a formal organization, but it is a clear group. Right now its home base is **Bilibili**: a few top streamers (**up主**) and their fans. The streamers do live streams and post videos. Fans watch the streams or videos and talk in the comment sections.\n\n## Who runs the site\n\nThe site would be run by those few top streamers. They are fairly well known and they already have experience managing fan groups. But they are not very comfortable with computers. They would be the **admins**.\n\nBesides them, there would be some invited guide writers: other up主 or experienced players. They would be **editors**. They can write guides, but they can't manage users.\n\n## Who reads it, and what they want\n\nAnyone who plays the game. They just read; they don't need an account. The Bazaar has a strong guide culture. Compared with MOBAs or FPS games, a card game is more about strategy than mechanics, so players need guides more than in other games.\n\n## What is broken right now\n\nEverything is on Bilibili, and it is all video or live streams. A video is not like a written guide: you can't read it in a few spare minutes, or when you can't turn the sound on. Clear-cut information like **end-game builds** (终局阵容) is hard to find inside a video. Right now most streamers make guides by talking over a PowerPoint. A forum-style website (like **旅法师营地**) would be a better channel for this.\n\n## What would make them say \"this is better\"\n\nThey don't have a website yet. The biggest advantage of a website is that the information is easy to get to.\n\n## What must not happen\n\nRegular members and admins must have very different permissions. Admins should be able to control all users and all post pages. Regular members should only be able to make posts and write comments. Admins want to review content: posts should be reviewed before they go up, but comments can be looser.\n\nThis is not the final design yet, so this is what I have for now.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":14,"oldLines":7,"newStart":14,"newLines":7,"lines":[" "," ## What is broken right now"," ","-Everything is on Bilibili, and it is all video or live streams. | ✅ 主播,不熟电脑 |\n| 谁来看,想找什么 | ✅ 所有玩家,找攻略 |\n| 现在哪里不好 | ✅ 视频难以碎片化阅读、没法静音看,终局阵容在视频里难定位 |\n| 怎样算\"好多了\" | ⚠️ 只有一句\"信息好找\",偏薄 |\n| 什么绝对不能发生 | ✅ 改完后具体了,可以直接变成权限规则 |\n\n**评分项 A2(客户具体性,3 分):** 这是强项。B 站、up 主、对着 **管理后台**:内容列表按草稿/已发布筛选,admin 用它找待审核的攻略。\n- **公开网站**:只显示已发布的攻略。\n- **页面(pages)**:这一项目前**没有对应内容**,见下面第 1 点。\n\n**还有 3 个薄弱点,建议你改的时候补一补:**\n\n1. **Pages 放什么?** 手册要求已发布的页面出现在导航菜单里。攻略是 posts,那 pages 可以是\"新手入门\"、\"英雄总览\"、\"关于我们\"这类固定页面。简介里提一句就够,比如新手常问的那几个问题。\n2. **\"好多了\"太薄。** 能不能具体一点?比如\"玩家想查某个英雄的终局阵容,30 秒内就能找到,不用拖视频进度条\"。具体的场景比抽象的\"信息好获取\"更有说服力。\n3. **一个值得想的矛盾:** 你写了主播\"对电脑不熟\",但这个项目的编辑器要求用 Markdown 写正文,而所见即所得的富文本编辑器被明确排除了。不熟电脑的人怎么写 Markdown?不用现在解决,这正是 grill 时的好题目,你也可以先在简介里点出来。\n\n这 3 点都是补充内容,你可以用中文告诉我,我出英文后加进草稿;也可以直接在 VS Code 里自己写。改完告诉我,我放进 {"parentUuid":"072b4519-f47f-4e6e-afc3-fac3886af924","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"f0be7572-a6ce-4bf0-8a80-2653ac94c90f","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"pages可以有“攻略”，“锦标赛”，“关于”这几项，其中攻略可以按照作者检索，也可以按照英雄检索。英雄比较好理解，然后作者我预计不会太多，所以也可以这样检索。好多了指的就是我现在想找一个特定版本的某个英雄的攻略，只能通过Bilibili的视频查找，问题是全局视频很长，我很难直接定位到我想要的阵容。而这种roguelike游戏每局都不一样，甚至一局游戏阵容也会变来变去，我很难获取到我想要的信息。而现有的攻略类视频是对着ppt讲的这种视频，有效信息其实只是图片和up说的话，这样明显不如post直观，想说的话直接写成文字，ppt里的图片直接放到post里面，这样对观众和制作者来说都是一种简化。第三个问题其实很好解决，因为众多Up主肯定有会写的，而即使真的一个都没有，也完全可以借助AI来转化，这不是一个难事。那假如我按照项目要求给columbus那个三个人的公益组织设计网页，他们三个就一定有懂电脑的吗？"},"uuid":"de5dd5c4-ff15-45a1-ba56-b15b1f649430","timestamp":"2026-10-16T04:31:51.167Z","permissionMode":"bypassPermissions","origin":{"kind":"human"},"promptSource":"typed","turnOrigin":"human","turnPosition":{"promptIndex":23,"turnIndex":24},"userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}
