Among all the up主 there will definitely be some who can do it, and even if none of them can, they can easily use AI to convert their text.","originalFile":"# Client brief — The Bazaar Chinese community\n\nThe client is the Chinese-speaking player community of **The Bazaar** (大巴扎). It is not a formal organization, but it is a clear group. Right now its home base is **Bilibili**: a few top streamers (**up主**) and their fans. The streamers do live streams and post videos. Fans watch the streams or videos and talk in the comment sections.\n\n## Who runs the site\n\nThe site would be run by those few top streamers. They are fairly well known and they already have experience managing fan groups. But they are not very comfortable with computers. They would be the **admins**.\n\nBesides them, there would be some invited guide writers: other up主 or experienced players. They would be **editors**. They can write guides, but they can't manage users.\n\n## Who reads it, and what they want\n\nAnyone who plays the game. They just read; they don't need an account. The Bazaar has a strong guide culture. Compared with MOBAs or FPS games, a card game is more about strategy than mechanics, so players need guides more than in other games.\n\n## What is broken right now\n\nEverything is on Bilibili, and it is all video or live streams. A video is not like a written guide: you can't read it in a few spare minutes, or when you can't turn the sound on. Clear-cut information like **end-game builds** (终局阵容) is hard to find inside a video. Right now most streamers make guides by talking over a PowerPoint. A website with written guides (something like **旅法师营地**) would be a better channel for this. Comments and discussion can stay on Bilibili.\n\n## What would make them say \"this is better\"\n\nThey don't have a website yet. The biggest advantage of a website is that the information is easy to get to.\n\n## What must not happen\n\nEditors and admins must have very different permissions. Admins should be able to control all users and all posts and pages. Editors should only be able to write guides. An editor must never be able to manage users or publish something that an admin hasn't reviewed: an editor's guide stays a draft until an admin checks it and publishes it.\n\nThis is not the final design yet, so this is what I have for now.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":8,"oldLines":6,"newStart":8,"newLines":8,"lines":[" "," Besides them, there would be some invited guide writers: other up主 or experienced players. They would be **editors**. They can write guides, but they can't manage users."," ","+Writing in Markdown shouldn't be a big problem. Among all the up主 there will definitely be some who can do it, and even if none of them can, they can easily use AI to convert their text.","+"," ## Who reads it, and what they want"," "," Anyone who plays the game. They just read; they don't need an account. The Bazaar has a strong guide culture. Compared with MOBAs or FPS games, a card game is more about strategy than mechanics, so players need guides more than in other games."]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"10a70e46-c982-4801-af17-3733d00e5620","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

The biggest advantage of a website is that the information is easy to get to.\n\nSay I want a guide for a specific hero on a specific patch. Right now I can only search Bilibili videos, and the videos are long, so it's hard to jump straight to the build I want. The Bazaar is a roguelike, so every run is different, and even inside one run the build keeps changing. That makes it really hard to get the information I need.\n\nThe existing guide videos are just someone talking over a PowerPoint. The useful information is only the pictures and what the up主 says. A post is clearly more direct: what they want to say can be written as text, and the pictures from the PowerPoint can go straight into the post. That is simpler for both the viewers and the people making guides.\n\nThe site would have three main pages in the menu: **Guides** (攻略), **Tournaments** (锦标赛), and **About** (关于). Guides can be browsed by **hero** or by **author**. Hero is the obvious one. I expect there won't be too many authors, so browsing by author works too.","originalFile":"# Client brief — The Bazaar Chinese community\n\nThe client is the Chinese-speaking player community of **The Bazaar** (大巴扎). It is not a formal organization, but it is a clear group. Right now its home base is **Bilibili**: a few top streamers (**up主**) and their fans. The streamers do live streams and post videos. Fans watch the streams or videos and talk in the comment sections.\n\n## Who runs the site\n\nThe site would be run by those few top streamers. They are fairly well known and they already have experience managing fan groups. But they are not very comfortable with computers. They would be the **admins**.\n\nBesides them, there would be some invited guide writers: other up主 or experienced players. They would be **editors**. They can write guides, but they can't manage users.\n\nWriting in Markdown shouldn't be a big problem. Among all the up主 there will definitely be some who can do it, and even if none of them can, they can easily use AI to convert their text.\n\n## Who reads it, and what they want\n\nAnyone who plays the game. They just read; they don't need an account. The Bazaar has a strong guide culture. Compared with MOBAs or FPS games, a card game is more about strategy than mechanics, so players need guides more than in other games.\n\n## What is broken right now\n\nEverything is on Bilibili, and it is all video or live streams. A video is not like a written guide: you can't read it in a few spare minutes, or when you can't turn the sound on. Clear-cut information like **end-game builds** (终局阵容) is hard to find inside a video. Right now most streamers make guides by talking over a PowerPoint. A website with written guides (something like **旅法师营地**) would be a better channel for this. Comments and discussion can stay on Bilibili.\n\n## What would make them say \"this is better\"\n\nThey don't have a website yet. The biggest advantage of a website is that the information is easy to get to.\n\n## What must not happen\n\nEditors and admins must have very different permissions. Admins should be able to control all users and all posts and pages. Editors should only be able to write guides. An editor must never be able to manage users or publish something that an admin hasn't reviewed: an editor's guide stays a draft until an admin checks it and publishes it.\n\nThis is not the final design yet, so this is what I have for now.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":22,"oldLines":6,"newStart":22,"newLines":12,"lines":[" "," They don't have a website yet. The biggest advantage of a website is that the information is easy to get to."," ","+Say I want a guide for a specific hero on a specific patch. 的所有攻略\"这种页面,效果类似检索。这在 7 项必做功能之外,但不算大,也确实符合你的客户需求,grill 时决定做到什么程度。\n2. **你提到\"特定版本\"**,这是一个很好的细节。攻略会随游戏版本过时,所以攻略可能需要一个\"版本号\"字段。我没写进简介,只在\"好多了\"那段保留了你的原话\"specific patch\",留到 grill 时再细问。\n\n**篇幅:** 草稿现在比手册说的\"半页\"长一些。可以接受,内容都是你的,但你改的时候如果想删,\"现在哪里不好\"和\"好多了\"两段有一点重复,可以合并。\n\n改完保存,告诉我\"改好了\",我放进 When I look for a guide, unless it was just posted, it's hard to say how much it still applies.","originalFile":"# Client brief — The Bazaar Chinese community\n\nThe client is the Chinese-speaking player community of **The Bazaar** (大巴扎). It is not a formal organization, but it is a clear group. Right now its home base is **Bilibili**: a few top streamers (**up主**) and their fans. The streamers do live streams and post videos. Fans watch the streams or videos and talk in the comment sections.\n\n## Who runs the site\n\nThe site would be run by those few top streamers. They are fairly well known and they already have experience managing fan groups. But they are not very comfortable with computers. They would be the **admins**.\n\nBesides them, there would be some invited guide writers: other up主 or experienced players. They would be **editors**. They can write guides, but they can't manage users.\n\nWriting in Markdown shouldn't be a big problem. Among all the up主 there will definitely be some who can do it, and even if none of them can, they can easily use AI to convert their text.\n\n## Who reads it, and what they want\n\nAnyone who plays the game. They just read; they don't need an account. The Bazaar has a strong guide culture. Compared with MOBAs or FPS games, a card game is more about strategy than mechanics, so players need guides more than in other games.\n\n## What is broken right now\n\nEverything is on Bilibili, and it is all video or live streams. A video is not like a written guide: you can't read it in a few spare minutes, or when you can't turn the sound on. Clear-cut information like **end-game builds** (终局阵容) is hard to find inside a video. Right now most streamers make guides by talking over a PowerPoint. A website with written guides (something like **旅法师营地**) would be a better channel for this. Comments and discussion can stay on Bilibili.\n\n## What would make them say \"this is better\"\n\nThey don't have a website yet. The biggest advantage of a website is that the information is easy to get to.\n\nSay I want a guide for a specific hero on a specific patch. Right now I can only search Bilibili videos, and the videos are long, so it's hard to jump straight to the build I want. The Bazaar is a roguelike, so every run is different, and even inside one run the build keeps changing. That makes it really hard to get the information I need.\n\nThe existing guide videos are just someone talking over a PowerPoint. The useful information is only the pictures and what the up主 says. A post is clearly more direct: what they want to say can be written as text, and the pictures from the PowerPoint can go straight into the post. That is simpler for both the viewers and the people making guides.\n\nThe site would have three main pages in the menu: **Guides** (攻略), **Tournaments** (锦标赛), and **About** (关于). Guides can be browsed by **hero** or by **author**. Hero is the obvious one. I expect there won't be too many authors, so browsing by author works too.\n\n## What must not happen\n\nEditors and admins must have very different permissions. Admins should be able to control all users and all posts and pages. Editors should only be able to write guides. An editor must never be able to manage users or publish something that an admin hasn't reviewed: an editor's guide stays a draft until an admin checks it and publishes it.\n\nThis is not the final design yet, so this is what I have for now.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":18,"oldLines":6,"newStart":18,"newLines":8,"lines":[" "," Everything is on Bilibili, and it is all video or live streams. A video is not like a written guide: you can't read it in a few spare minutes, or when you can't turn the sound on. Clear-cut information like **end-game builds** (终局阵容) is hard to find inside a video. Right now most streamers make guides by talking over a PowerPoint. A website with written guides (something like **旅法师营地**) would be a better channel for this. Comments and discussion can stay on Bilibili."," ","+Timing is another big problem. The game gets **balance patches** that make cards stronger or weaker, on average about twice a month. Videos cost a lot to make (a single author might only post one or two a month), so they go out of date fast. When I look for a guide, unless it was just posted, it's hard to say how much it still applies.","+"," ## What would make them say \"this is better\""," "," They don't have a website yet. The biggest advantage of a website is that the information is easy to get to."]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"22d807f6-73c7-4838-8d7d-71b844ce8347","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"type":"last-prompt","lastPrompt":"对于特定版本，我想补充的是游戏因为平衡性原因经常会有平衡补丁调整卡牌强弱，平均一个月会有两回，这也就导致了制作成本极大的视频（比如单一作者一个月也就发一两个视频）时效性很差，而我想找攻略，除非是刚刚发布的，否则很难说有什么参考性","leafUuid":"cbf7dc58-7f15-4266-ab8b-6ec174d76152","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf"}

{"parentUuid":"03a78ed1-6fc6-4a21-872d-b78efc3e95b5","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg5J5SGjExhR6iSs52VcT","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"加进去了,放在\"现在哪里不好\"那一节的末尾,作为单独一段:平衡补丁平均一个月两次,视频制作成本高、一个作者一个月只发一两个,所以视频很快就过时,除非是刚发布的,否则很难判断还有没有参考价值。\n\n这一条让你的论点更完整了。之前的论点是\"视频不好找\",现在多了一条\"视频跟不上更新\"。文字攻略的优势就很清楚:补丁出来后改几行字就行,不用重新录一整个视频。\n\n它也基本确定了 grill 时要讨论的一个设计点:攻略要不要标版本号,公开网站上要不要显示\"这篇攻略适用于哪个版本\"。按你的描述,这对读者判断一篇攻略能不能信很关键。\n\n你在 VS Code 里改完保存,告诉我\"改好了\",我放进 `notes/client-brief.md`。"}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":565,"cache_read_input_tokens":124372,"output_tokens":312,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":565,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":312,"cache_read_input_tokens":124372,"cache_creation_input_tokens":565,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":565},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011Cg5J5Rx8Rm7ML6dWnv1jG","type":"assistant","uuid":"b9d2ea7c-4610-48e6-baba-7f03490e5fa7","timestamp":"2026-10-16T04:36:16.919Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

时用得上。你的\"按英雄、按作者浏览\"其实就是 taxonomy。\n2. **练习 A、练习 B**:两个小编程练习,和客户无关,随时可做。\n3. **grill**:正式开始设计。手册要求在全新会话里做,这时候就该用 `/clear` 了。\n\n我建议按 1 → grill → 再穿插 A、B 的顺序做。grill 时你脑子里还有刚写完简介的新鲜感,回答会更具体。A 和 B 是机械性的工作,累了的时候做正好。\n\n先提交吗?commit {"parentUuid":"0273be52-6517-4dfe-8ba7-4c8fdf139589","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg5KtAqUE7JXZrsGFX2jD","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01YS2bWN7gCEigwzvs92Y4rr","name":"Agent","input":{"description":"Research CMS content vocabulary","subagent_type":"general-purpose","model":"sonnet","prompt":"Research task for a student course project (IPHS 400 Mini-Project 2: a small web CMS). Write ONE Markdown file and nothing else; do not modify any other file, do not commit.\n\nQuestion: How do content management systems model content, users and roles, and publishing? Compare WordPress, Drupal, and static-site generators (Hugo, Jekyll, Eleventy — pick the two best documented). Explain each of these terms as each system uses it: content type, slug, draft/published (post status), role, capability/permission, permalink, taxonomy (categories/tags/custom taxonomies; Drupal vocabularies/terms; Hugo taxonomies), theme, headless CMS.\n\nRules:\n- Use primary sources only: official documentation (developer.wordpress.org, wordpress.org/documentation, drupal.org/docs, gohugo.io/documentation, jekyllrb.com/docs, 11ty.dev/docs), source code, or specs. Do not cite blogs, tutorials, or Wikipedia. Cite the source URL for every claim inline. If you could not verify something from a primary source, say so instead of guessing.\n- Keep it compact: aim for about 1200–1800 words. A comparison table of the terms across systems is welcome.\n- Write in plain English, short sentences.\n\nProject context (use it for a short final section \"What this means for our project\", 5–8 bullets, clearly marked as suggestions, not decisions): the CMS is FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, with a local-only admin console and a static public site exported to GitHub Pages (`cms publish` renders only published rows to HTML with relative paths). Two roles: admin and editor. Content: posts and pages, with title, slug, Markdown body, draft/published, author, timestamps; published pages appear in public navigation. This is the project.**\n422\t\n423\t### 6.1 Grill (one session, fresh window)\n424\t\n425\t```text\n426\t/clear\n427\t/grill-with-docs I am building a small CMS for <your client, in one sentence>. Here are my field notes: notes/cms-field-notes.md and my brief: notes/client-brief.md. The 7 required capabilities are in the manual; help me decide what they mean for this client.\n428\t```\n429\t\n430\tIt asks **one question at a time**, with a recommended answer attached. How to be good at this:\n431\t\n432\t- **Answer with your client's reality**, not with generalities. \"Karen posts weekly and will never remember a slug\" is worth more than \"yes, sounds good.\"\n433\t- **Override the recommendation when you disagree**, and say why. That sentence is the single strongest evidence of your own judgment, and factor A samples exactly these answers.\n434\t- **Watch `CONTEXT.md` fill up** as terms resolve. It is a bit over the 1800-word target, at roughly 2,300 words. I changed no other file, and I did not commit or touch `.claude/state/phase`.\n\nIt covers WordPress, Drupal, Hugo and Jekyll. Eleventy gets one short note on tag collections and pagination. It has a comparison table, one section per system, and 9 suggestion bullets under \"What this means for our project\". That is one more than the 5–8 you asked for. Every claim has its source URL inline, and a final section lists what I could not verify.\n\n1. **Contributor vs Editor:** WordPress Contributors can write but \"cannot publish\". A post from a user with `edit_posts` but not `publish_posts` gets the `pending` status. The pages are https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/roles-and-capabilities/ and https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/post-status/. Our \"editor\" role is closer to WordPress's Contributor, and `pending` fits the admin-review flow.\n2. **Roles are bundles of capabilities:** WordPress calls them capabilities and Drupal calls them permissions. Hugo and Jekyll have no users or roles that I could find. I suggest checking capabilities in the code, not role names.\n3. **Per-term pages:** Hugo's taxonomies build a terms index plus one list page per term (`taxonomy.html` and `term.html`). That is a good model for per-hero and per-author pages in `cms publish`. Jekyll's docs describe no built-in per-tag pages. Eleventy builds them with pagination.\n4. **Hugo's \"permalink\" is an absolute URL:** The glossary says it includes scheme and host. Its `relativeURLs` option is described as useful only for serverless sites. It is a bit over the 1800-word target, at roughly 2,300 words. I changed no other file, and I did not commit or touch `.claude/state/phase`.\n\nIt covers WordPress, Drupal, Hugo and Jekyll. Eleventy gets one short note on tag collections and pagination. It has a comparison table, one section per system, and 9 suggestion bullets under \"What this means for our project\". That is one more than the 5–8 you asked for. Every claim has its source URL inline, and a final section lists what I could not verify.\n\n1. **Contributor vs Editor:** WordPress Contributors can write but \"cannot publish\". A post from a user with `edit_posts` but not `publish_posts` gets the `pending` status. The pages are https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/roles-and-capabilities/ and https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/post-status/. Our \"editor\" role is closer to WordPress's Contributor, and `pending` fits the admin-review flow.\n2. **Roles are bundles of capabilities:** WordPress calls them capabilities and Drupal calls them permissions. Hugo and Jekyll have no users or roles that I could find. I suggest checking capabilities in the code, not role names.\n3. **Per-term pages:** Hugo's taxonomies build a terms index plus one list page per term (`taxonomy.html` and `term.html`). That is a good model for per-hero and per-author pages in `cms publish`. Jekyll's docs describe no built-in per-tag pages. Eleventy builds them with pagination.\n4. **Hugo's \"permalink\" is an absolute URL:** The glossary says it includes scheme and host. Its `relativeURLs` option is described as useful only for serverless sites. {"parentUuid":"0e1cf02e-5f39-4db2-a52b-ee7ebdca45c4","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"fcc50f35-c71c-4ee3-b52f-482c5a094542","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Aj99BNkLkfS6jxKyeiNGAh","type":"tool_result","content":"123\t## 7. What this means for our project\n124\t\n125\tThese are suggestions, not decisions.\n126\t\n127\t- **Borrow WordPress's status split.** Use `draft`, `pending`, `published`. WordPress's `pending` means \"awaiting a user with the `publish_posts` capability\". That matches the client's \"admin reviews editor guides\" flow.\n128\t- **Use two or three capabilities, not role checks everywhere.** For example `edit_own`, `edit_any`, `publish`. Roles are bundles of these. WordPress does it this way, and Drupal does it the same way with \"permissions\". Editor gets the first, admin gets all three. Route code checks the capability. Then the rule can change without touching routes.\n129\t- **Treat our \"editor\" like WordPress's Contributor, not WordPress's Editor.** In WordPress, Contributor can write but \"cannot publish\" their posts, and WordPress Editor can publish others' posts. Our editor is closer to a Contributor.\n130\t- **Hero and author as taxonomies.** Hugo's model fits: a taxonomy (`hero`, `author`) has terms, and content is assigned to terms. Hugo builds one list page per term and a terms index. Our `cms publish` could do the same with Jinja: loop over each hero and write `heroes/<slug>/index.html` with its published guides. Hugo's templates are `taxonomy.html` and `term.html`. WordPress and Drupal have the same idea (terms, vocabularies).\n131\t- **Author may not need to be a taxonomy table.** It is already a user relation. A per-author list page can come from the `author` column. Hero can be a small table with a slug and a Chinese display name. Both give the same output page shape.\n132\t- **Slugs must be decided early.** All four systems derive a slug from a title and use it in the URL. The WordPress slug function keeps only letters, digits, underscore and dash. I did not verify what happens to Chinese titles. For a Chinese-speaking audience, consider that a slug is typed or edited by the writer, ASCII or pinyin, and unique per type. This is a design risk to test, not a documented answer.\n133\t- **Keep paths relative.** Hugo's \"permalink\" is absolute by definition, and its relative mode is described as niche. Our hard rule (no `href=\"/...\"`) means we compute relative paths ourselves, depending on page depth. Per-term pages like `heroes/<slug>/` are one level deeper than the home page.\n134\t- **Patch version field.** None of the systems has a built-in \"patch version\". It is just a custom field: Drupal fields, WordPress custom fields/post meta, Hugo front matter. A plain `patch_version` column on posts, shown on the page and used to flag stale guides, matches what the others do. Hugo's `expiryDate` is a related idea (stop rendering after a date), but a patch version fits balance patches better. That comparison is my own.\n135\t- **Navigation from published pages.** Hugo adds a page to a menu with `menus: main` in front matter. We could use a `show_in_nav` flag on pages, with the public nav built only from published rows.\n136\t- **Headless is optional.** A static export is a stronger form of decoupling than a headless API. Our admin is the content backend and the site is a build output. We do not need a public API.\n137\t\n138\t## 8. Gaps\n139\t\n140\t- Drupal: no \"slug\", \"permalink\" or \"content editor\" role definition found. Drupal's theme page on `drupal.org` redirects in some docs paths, so I used the User Guide URL that returned content.\n141\t- WordPress: no official definition of \"headless\" found.\n142\t- Hugo and Jekyll: no definition of roles or capabilities found, and none of \"headless CMS\".\n143\t- Jekyll: whether it can build per-term pages without a plugin is not stated on the pages I read.\n144\t- Chinese-character slug behavior: not verified for any system.\n145\t"}]},"uuid":"727bacd1-63e1-4ceb-af53-34428cf4fde3","timestamp":"2026-10-16T05:02:48.936Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/notes/research-cms-vocabulary.md","content":"## 7. What this means for our project\n\nThese are suggestions, not decisions.\n\n- **Borrow WordPress's status split.** Use `draft`, `pending`, `published`. WordPress's `pending` means \"awaiting a user with the `publish_posts` capability\". That matches the client's \"admin reviews editor guides\" flow.\n- **Use two or three capabilities, not role checks everywhere.** For example `edit_own`, `edit_any`, `publish`. Roles are bundles of these. WordPress does it this way, and Drupal does it the same way with \"permissions\". Editor gets the first, admin gets all three. Route code checks the capability. Then the rule can change without touching routes.\n- **Treat our \"editor\" like WordPress's Contributor, not WordPress's Editor.** In WordPress, Contributor can write but \"cannot publish\" their posts, and WordPress Editor can publish others' posts. Our editor is closer to a Contributor.\n- **Hero and author as taxonomies.** Hugo's model fits: a taxonomy (`hero`, `author`) has terms, and content is assigned to terms. Hugo builds one list page per term and a terms index. Our `cms publish` could do the same with Jinja: loop over each hero and write `heroes/<slug>/index.html` with its published guides. Hugo's templates are `taxonomy.html` and `term.html`. WordPress and Drupal have the same idea (terms, vocabularies).\n- **Author may not need to be a taxonomy table.** It is already a user relation. A per-author list page can come from the `author` column. Hero can be a small table with a slug and a Chinese display name. Both give the same output page shape.\n- **Slugs must be decided early.** All four systems derive a slug from a title and use it in the URL. The WordPress slug function keeps only letters, digits, underscore and dash. I did not verify what happens to Chinese titles. For a Chinese-speaking audience, consider that a slug is typed or edited by the writer, ASCII or pinyin, and unique per type. This is a design risk to test, not a documented answer.\n- **Keep paths relative.** Hugo's \"permalink\" is absolute by definition, and its relative mode is described as niche. Our hard rule (no `href=\"/...\"`) means we compute relative paths ourselves, depending on page depth. Per-term pages like `heroes/<slug>/` are one level deeper than the home page.\n- **Patch version field.** None of the systems has a built-in \"patch version\". It is just a custom field: Drupal fields, WordPress custom fields/post meta, Hugo front matter. A plain `patch_version` column on posts, shown on the page and used to flag stale guides, matches what the others do. Hugo's `expiryDate` is a related idea (stop rendering after a date), but a patch version fits balance patches better. That comparison is my own.\n- **Navigation from published pages.** Hugo adds a page to a menu with `menus: main` in front matter. We could use a `show_in_nav` flag on pages, with the public nav built only from published rows.\n- **Headless is optional.** A static export is a stronger form of decoupling than a headless API. Our admin is the content backend and the site is a build output. We do not need a public API.\n\n## 8. Gaps\n\n- Drupal: no \"slug\", \"permalink\" or \"content editor\" role definition found. Drupal's theme page on `drupal.org` redirects in some docs paths, so I used the User Guide URL that returned content.\n- WordPress: no official definition of \"headless\" found.\n- Hugo and Jekyll: no definition of roles or capabilities found, and none of \"headless CMS\".\n- Jekyll: whether it can build per-term pages without a plugin is not stated on the pages I read.\n- Chinese-character slug behavior: not verified for any system.\n","numLines":23,"startLine":123,"totalLines":145}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"0e1cf02e-5f39-4db2-a52b-ee7ebdca45c4","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"c00fcf57-d0c2-4d04-9977-514e180396c6","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg5L7VCtMSkTQBrDu64Rp","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Part 2.3 的术语研究做完了,已经提交(`5dd076c`)。文件是 `notes/research-cms-vocabulary.md`,对比了 WordPress、Drupal、Hugo、Jekyll,每条结论都附了官方文档链接,共引用 36 处。\n\n**对你的项目最有用的 5 点,grill 时都用得上:**\n\n1. **你的 editor 更像 WordPress 的 Contributor,而不是 WordPress 的 Editor。** 在 WordPress 里,Contributor 能写但不能发布,文章会进入 `pending`(待审核)状态,由有发布权限的人批准。这和你\"editor 写的攻略要 admin 审核\"完全一致。所以文章状态可能是三种:草稿、待审核、已发布,而不是两种。\n2. **\"按英雄浏览\"在 CMS 里叫 taxonomy(分类法)。** 静态网站生成器 Hugo 的做法是给每个英雄生成一个列表页,比如 `heroes/vanessa/`。你的 `cms publish` 可以照这个做。\n3. **\"按作者浏览\"不用额外建分类。** 每篇攻略本来就有作者字段,直接按作者生成列表页就行。\n4. **版本号没有现成的标准做法**,所有系统都用自定义字段。给攻略加一个 `patch_version` 字段,在页面上显示,用来标记过时的攻略,就够了。\n5. **中文标题怎么变成网址(slug)是一个未知风险。** WordPress 的 slug 只保留字母、数字、下划线和短横线,中文标题会怎样没有查到。grill 时要定:slug 用拼音、英文,还是作者自己填。\n\n## 下一步:grill\n\n研究结果已经存进文件,现在可以清空上下文了。请依次输入:\n\n```text\n/clear\n```\n```text\n/grill-with-docs I am building a small CMS for the Chinese-speaking community of the card game The Bazaar, so streamers and invited writers can publish written guides that players can browse by hero and author. Here are my field notes: notes/cms-field-notes.md, my brief: notes/client-brief.md, and my research: notes/research-cms-vocabulary.md. The 7 required capabilities are in docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md (Part 3.3); help me decide what they mean for this client.\n```\n\n和上一条比,这次的命令多附了研究文件。描述客户的那一句可以改成你自己的说法。\n\n**提醒:**\n- 进入 grill 后,我会先把阶段标签改成 `grill`。\n- 用英文回答,带上你客户的真实细节。不同意我的推荐时就直接说,并给出理由。\n- 可以在 VS Code 里打开 `CONTEXT.md`,看术语表随着讨论慢慢填满。"}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":390,"cache_read_input_tokens":137967,"output_tokens":973,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":390,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":973,"cache_read_input_tokens":137967,"cache_creation_input_tokens":390,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":390},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011Cg5L7UumAHSjbeEzPBoNx","type":"assistant","uuid":"b54ece4f-fb08-48c3-8ab7-349c557e5f9d","timestamp":"2026-10-16T05:03:04.786Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

Saving them automatically means\nyou cannot forget — in MP1 nobody remembered. The name follows the required\npattern; set CMS_STUDENT=first-last in .env (or your shell) so it is right.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport re\nimport shutil\nimport sys\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n\ndef student_slug(project: Path) -> str:\n    name = os.environ.get(\"CMS_STUDENT\")\n    if not name:\n        env = project / \".env\"\n        if env.exists():\n            match = re.search(r\"^CMS_STUDENT=(.+)$\", env.read_text(), re.M)\n            name = match.group(1).strip() if match else None\n    return re.sub(r\"[^a-z-]\", \"\", (name or \"your-name\").lower().replace(\" \", \"-\"))\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    event = json.load(sys.stdin)\n    source = Path(event.get(\"transcript_path\", \"\"))\n    if not source.exists():\n        return\n    project = Path(os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\") or event.get(\"cwd\") or \".\")\n    out = project / \"docs\" / \"transcripts\"\n    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    number = f\"{len(list(out.glob('*.md'))) + 1:02d}\"\n    target = out / (f\"iphs400_mp2-cms_chat-session_{number}_\"\n                    f\"{student_slug(project)}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d')}.md\")\n    if not target.exists():","numLines":40,"startLine":1,"totalLines":50}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"003bbfb6-29a8-4690-866d-a12fc7e9faa4","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"2f45b302-22a7-471e-b4b4-443b16f8f429","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg65awt1W31yqv5umWkuJ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"先讲流程和评分,再回答你关于开窗口的问题。最后有一件事需要你现在处理。\n\n## 整体流程\n\n```\n① field notes + 客户简介   ✅ 已完成\n② 术语研究                 ✅ 已完成\n③ grill(访谈)            → 产出 CONTEXT.md 术语表,可能有 ADR\n④ /to-spec                 → GitHub 上一个 spec issue\n⑤ /to-tickets              → 7–9 个 ticket issue\n   ※ 写 token 预算计划,必须在第一个 /implement 之前提交\n⑥ 每个工单:/clear → /implement #N → /code-review → 把审查意见贴到 issue → commit \"Closes #N\"\n⑦ 做完前 3 个工单 → 发布到 GitHub Pages → 打 mp2-mvp 标签\n⑧ 做完全部工单 → 截图、报告、README → 打 mp2-final 标签\n```\n\n练习 A、B 可以插在任何时候做,但预算计划(练习 B 的一部分)必须在 ⑥ 之前提交,这是评分项 B7a。\n\n## 评分\n\n总分 100 分:Stage 1 占 15 分,Stage 2 占 85 分,**70 分及格**(Pass/No-Pass)。\n\n| 类别 | 分值 | 主要看什么 |\n|---|---|---|\n| A 是不是你本人的判断 | 17 | grill 回答(5)、客户具体性(3)、报告口吻(4)、AI 使用声明(3)、你自己写的 commit 和评论(2) |\n| B 工作流程 | 17 | 先 spec 后 tickets、每个工单都有审查、会话纪律、token 预算 |\n| C 功能 | 15 | 7 项功能逐项实测 |\n| D 安全 | 8 | 密码哈希、CSRF、权限测试、Markdown 过滤 |\n| E 测试和代码质量 | 8 | 测试全过、测试对应验收标准 |\n| F 网站和后台体验 | 7 | HTTPS、无坏链接、手机宽度不溢出 |\n| G 报告和文档 | 6 | 报告回答 4 个问题、README、12 张截图 |\n| H 合规完整 | 7 | 文件齐全 |\n\n**评分标准的原话是:大量使用 AI 是预期之内的,扣分的是没经过编辑的 AI 文字。**\n\n## grill 是什么\n\ngrill 不是\"反复提要求、反复修改\",而是**一场访谈**:\n- 我一次只问一个问题,每个问题附一个我推荐的答案。\n- 你可以接受、反驳,或者补充你客户的情况。\n- 每定下一个术语,我就写进 `CONTEXT.md`。\n- 等你能毫不含糊地回答下面这几件事,grill 就结束:这里的 post 是什么,page 是什么,谁能做什么,\"发布\"是什么意思,哪些明确不做。\n\n**A1(5 分)是这样评的:** 从 grill 记录里抽 10 条你的回答,数有几条做到了下面任意一点:\n- 补充了问题里没有的、关于你客户的事实、限制或偏好;\n- 推翻了我的推荐答案,并给出理由。\n\n7 条以上满分。只回答 \"yes, sounds good\" 的那条就不算。\n\n## 另开一个窗口商量,违反规则吗?\n\n**不违反。** 规则里没有禁止。但有两件事你要知道:\n\n1. **每个会话都会被自动存档并提交。** 项目里的 `save_transcript.py` 钩子会在每个会话结束时,把完整对话复制到 `docs/transcripts/`,评分时会读。所以商量用的那个窗口也会被看到。这本身没问题,反而更透明。\n2. **界限是:商量可以,代写答案不行。** 在另一个窗口问\"这个问题是什么意思\"、\"这两种做法各有什么利弊\",完全没问题,相当于问助教。但如果我在那边替你写好答案、你再贴进 grill,就违背了 A1 要衡量的东西(\"回答是你自己的\"),而且评分人能在两份记录里看到这个过程。\n\n**更简单的办法:直接在 grill 窗口里问。** 遇到看不懂的问题,就在 grill 里说\"我不懂这个,能解释一下吗\",或者用 `/wait-what` 让我换个说法再讲一遍。我解释完你再回答。这样理解过程也留在 grill 记录里,能证明你是想清楚之后才做的决定。另开窗口留给 grill 之外的大问题。\n\n## ⚠️ 现在需要你做一件事\n\ntranscript 文件名要求是 `..._{first}-{last}_{日期}.md`,名字从 `.env` 里的 `CMS_STUDENT` 读取。但你的项目里**还没有 `.env` 文件**,所以现在存档的文件名会变成 `your-name`,`check_submission.py` 会判不合格。\n\n告诉我你的名和姓(用英文拼写,比如 `yining-chen`),我从 `.env.example` 复制一份 `.env`,把名字填进去。`.env` 已经被 git 忽略,不会被提交。这一步最好在你 `/clear` {"parentUuid":"548337b8-414e-4555-bc9f-f91fe1dfc8df","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg65pRU47KyAk9XR8vAKv","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"`.env` 建好了,里面有 `CMS_STUDENT=nick-chen`。我已经确认它被 git 忽略,不会被提交。以后的会话存档会自动命名为 `iphs400_mp2-cms_chat-session_NN_nick-chen_日期.md`。我还顺手把 `CMS_SECRET_KEY` 换成了一个随机生成的长字符串,模板里的默认值不安全。其他值暂时保留,网站标题等 grill 定下名字再改。\n\n**你的理解有一处要纠正:现在这个会话也会被记录。** 存档钩子对每个会话都生效,你一输入 `/clear`,这个会话就会结束并存档成第 01 号文件。它只是不算 grill:A1 只抽查 grill 会话里的回答,所以这里的中文对话不影响那 5 分。但评分人能看到这份记录,这没有问题,里面都是正常的讨论。\n\n**其他理解都对:**\n- grill 里我用全英文提问,你也用英文回答。\n- **英文不完美完全没关系。** A1 数的是你的回答里有没有你客户的事实、限制、偏好,或者有没有带理由的反驳,不看语法。简短、直接、有具体细节的英文,比流畅但空泛的英文得分高。\n- 实在不知道怎么说时,可以夹一个中文词,比如 \"the 终局阵容 (final build)\",或者问我 \"how do I say 平衡补丁 in English?\"。我只告诉你那个词,不会替你写整句。\n\n**开始 grill,请依次输入:**\n\n```text\n/clear\n```\n```text\n/grill-with-docs I am building a small CMS for the Chinese-speaking community of the card game The Bazaar, so streamers and invited writers can publish written guides that players can browse by hero and author. Here are my field notes: notes/cms-field-notes.md, my brief: notes/client-brief.md, and my research: notes/research-cms-vocabulary.md. The 7 required capabilities are in docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md (Part 3.3); help me decide what they mean for this client.\n```\n\n`/clear` 之后,我会忘掉这次对话的全部内容,只能从文件里读取:你的笔记、简介、研究、手册,还有 `CLAUDE.md`。这次谈到的关键点,比如 editor 的攻略需要 admin 审核、补丁一个月两次、评论留在 Bilibili,都已经写在简介里了,不会丢。"}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":497,"cache_read_input_tokens":149381,"output_tokens":913,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":55},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":497,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":913,"cache_read_input_tokens":149381,"cache_creation_input_tokens":497,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":497},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg65pR6yg759rTM9QAs5B","type":"assistant","uuid":"e4191881-4360-4dab-9b42-6a6b5811d4af","timestamp":"2026-10-16T14:36:13.200Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}
